name: Yang Zhiling
current_role: Founder and CEO, Moonshot AI (Beijing; maker of the Kimi chatbot and open-weight Kimi models)
profile: Yang Zhilin (b. 1992, Shantou) studied CS at Tsinghua and did a CMU PhD under Ruslan Salakhutdinov and William Cohen, co-authoring Transformer-XL and XLNet. After founding Recurrent AI, he co-founded Moonshot AI in 2023 with Tsinghua classmates; it raised ~$2B at a $20B+ valuation in May 2026 and has reportedly raised more since, ahead of a planned Hong Kong IPO.
interesting_fact: A prog-rock devotee, he named Moonshot AI in honour of Pink Floyd's album The Dark Side of the Moon; a white piano reportedly stands prominently in the Beijing office.
deep_cut_fact: At Tsinghua he was the drummer in a campus band called Splay and organised music competitions; he won admission there after taking first prize in China's National Olympiad in Informatics.
notes: Name usually romanised Yang Zhilin (杨植麟). Keeps a low profile: rarely gives interviews and has no public personal social-media account (Caixin). Best route is Moonshot's global PR address; X handle is the company's, not his.

name: Zhu Hongmei
current_role: Co-actual controller of Shenghong Group / Eastern Shenghong (000301.SZ); director of controlling shareholder Jiangsu Shenghong Technology
profile: Zhu Hongmei (朱红梅) is the wife and business partner of Miao Hangen, founder of Suzhou-based Shenghong Group; the couple are joint actual controllers of Eastern Shenghong. Shenghong grew over ~30 years from printing and dyeing in Shengze, Wujiang into polyester fibre, refining and petrochemicals (Shenghong Petrochemical in Lianyungang) and new-energy materials. She holds no executive post at the listed company.
interesting_fact: The couple took Shenghong public via a 2018 backdoor listing into Wujiang state-owned 'Oriental Market' (renamed Eastern Shenghong), reported as the largest A-share asset restructuring of 2018 and a mixed-ownership reform test case.
notes: Very private; virtually no personal public profile or interviews. Husband Miao Hangen (chairman of Shenghong/Eastern Shenghong) is the public face; best route is Eastern Shenghong's securities/IR office in Shengze, Suzhou (board secretary Wang Jun). Hurun lists wealth jointly with Miao Hangen.

name: Tench Coxe
current_role: Director, NVIDIA (since 1993; audit and compensation committees); former Managing Director, Sutter Hill Ventures
profile: Venture capitalist who joined Sutter Hill Ventures in 1987 and was managing director 1989-2020, focused on IT investments. Sutter Hill backed Nvidia at its founding and Coxe has sat on Nvidia's board since 1993; his stake made him a billionaire as Nvidia became the AI-datacenter giant. Now Austin-based, he is a philanthropist and was an Artisan Partners director until 2025.
interesting_fact: In January 2026 he and his wife Simone gave $100M, unrestricted, to launch UT Austin's new academic medical center (with an MD Anderson expansion) - one of the largest gifts in the university's history.
deep_cut_fact: Before venture capital he was Director of Marketing and MIS at Digital Communication Associates; he holds an economics BA from Dartmouth and a Harvard MBA. In 2025 he also became a minority owner of MLS club Austin FC.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Austin FC ownership: https://austinfc.com/news/austin-fc-announces-additions-to-clubs-ownership-group. Best formal route is Nvidia corporate PR; Austin philanthropy (UT/Dell Med) is a friendly hook.

name: Mike Adenuga
current_role: Chairman, Globacom (Glo) and Conoil; founder of Conoil Producing
profile: Nigerian tycoon (b. 1953) who made his first million at 26 trading lace and distributing soft drinks, then built Conoil Producing (oil blocks in the Niger Delta) and Globacom, a top-three Nigerian mobile operator that also built the Glo-1 submarine cable to the UK. Also owns 74% of listed fuel marketer Conoil and a stake in Sterling Financial Holdings.
interesting_fact: He paid his way through an MBA at Pace University in New York by working as a taxi driver; his Glo-1 cable runs about 6,100 miles from Nigeria to the UK via Ghana and Portugal.
deep_cut_fact: He personally funded the new Alliance Française de Lagos 'Mike Adenuga Centre' at 9 Osborne Road, Ikoyi: Emmanuel Macron inaugurated its first phase in July 2018 and it fully opened in May 2019, with an auditorium, library, art gallery and outdoor amphitheatre.
notes: Famously media-shy; rarely gives interviews and speaks via Globacom statements. No personal social accounts found. Turned 73 in April 2026. NCC has required Globacom to appoint a separate CEO (2025), so leadership structure may change; route via Globacom corporate communications.

name: Wang Qingtao
current_role: Founder/Chairman, Zhongrong Xinda Group (中融新大集团, formerly Shandong Coking Group), Qingdao — group in court-ordered bankruptcy restructuring since 2023
profile: Shandong-born (1962, Zouping) coal and coking entrepreneur known as the 'coking king'. Built Shandong Tiexiong Energy Coal Chemical from 2003, co-founded Shandong's largest coal-chemical park with Shagang in 2007, then renamed his group Zhongrong Xinda in 2016 and pivoted into bank stakes and mining (incl. a Peru iron mine). The group entered bankruptcy restructuring in 2023.
interesting_fact: Ranked Shandong's richest person on the 2021 New Fortune 500 list (RMB 59.65B), and was vice-chairman of the China Coking Industry Association.
deep_cut_fact: To win steel magnate Shen Wenrong's (Shagang) backing, he visited him in Jiangsu more than a dozen times in three months, telling him: 'You build the biggest steel mill, I'll build the biggest coking plant.' Earlier he served in the army and worked at the Zouping materials bureau before quitting to trade coal.
notes: Group in bankruptcy restructuring (Zibo Intermediate Court, 2023) and he reportedly faces numerous consumption-restriction orders; sensitive subject, not a likely podcast guest. No published personal/office contacts found. Also credited with a patented coke-oven smoke/dust removal device (cnpp.cn/focus/30788.html).

name: Eric Lefkofsky
current_role: Founder, CEO and Chairman, Tempus AI, Inc. (Nasdaq: TEM); cofounder of Lightbank
profile: Serial Chicago entrepreneur who made his fortune cofounding Groupon (2008) with Andrew Mason and longtime partner Brad Keywell, after earlier ventures including Starbelly, InnerWorkings, Echo Global Logistics and MediaOcean. Since 2015 he has run Tempus, which applies AI and molecular data to cancer care; it IPO'd in 2024 at about $6B, his fourth IPO. He also cofounded VC firm Lightbank.
interesting_fact: After a girlfriend dumped him in college at Michigan, he started his first business selling carpets, which he estimates generated hundreds of thousands of dollars in sales.
deep_cut_fact: He is a published author and longtime teacher: his 2007 book 'Accelerated Disruption' (Easton Studio Press) is about how technology reshapes business, and he has taught entrepreneurship/disruptive business models at Kellogg, DePaul and Chicago Booth.
notes: Personal site lefkofsky.com links his X and LinkedIn. Tempus media route is media@tempus.com. Strong AI/data angle (multimodal foundation models, large genomic datasets). Avoid personal/family health topics.

name: Xu Xin
current_role: Non-independent director (since July 2024) and co-actual controller, Hangzhou Changchuan Technology (300604.SZ)
profile: Xu Xin (徐昕, b. 1976) is co-actual controller, with chairman Zhao Yi (reported as her husband), of Hangzhou Changchuan Technology, a ChiNext-listed maker of chip test equipment (testers, handlers, AOI) founded 2008, listed 2017. She joined at founding as finance manager, later CFO and assistant GM; director since 2024.
interesting_fact: Changchuan has grown by buying foreign tool makers: Singapore AOI maker STI, the semiconductor division of Japan's SATO and Malaysia's test-equipment maker EXIS; it now employs about 4,500 people.
deep_cut_fact: Before Changchuan, she spent 1999-2005 as a sales clerk at Hangzhou Weili Trading; a Zhejiang Shuren University graduate, she joined Changchuan at its April 2008 founding as finance manager and ran its finances as CFO in 2015.
notes: Low public profile; husband Zhao Yi (ex-Silan Microelectronics production director, founder/chairman) is the public face. Best route is the company IR/board secretary office (secretary Shao Jingyang). Contacts are company-level, not personal.

name: Zhao Yi
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Hangzhou Changchuan Technology (CCTech, SZSE: 300604)
profile: Zhao Yi (b. 1976, Weiyuan, Neijiang, Sichuan) spent 1997-2007 at Hangzhou Silan Microelectronics, rising to production director, then founded Changchuan Technology in 2008 to make chip test and handling equipment (testers, handlers, probers, AOI). CCTech listed in Shenzhen in 2017; AI-driven demand for memory/advanced-packaging test pushed its market cap to ~CNY180B, and it is now pursuing a Hong Kong H-share listing.
interesting_fact: CCTech was billed as China's first listed semiconductor test-equipment company (Shenzhen ChiNext IPO, April 2017, at CNY9.94/share); its value rose from ~CNY27.7B to ~CNY180B in about 18 months to 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He started CCTech in April 2008 with just CNY500,000 in seed capital, launched its first gravity-type test handler that same year, and its in-house analog tester CTA8200 in 2009. The name 'Changchuan' combines the hometowns of the two co-founders: Changxing (Zhejiang) and Sichuan.
notes: Described in Chinese press as low-profile; co-founder and wife Xu Xin is a director (Hurun lists the fortune jointly). Board secretary Shao Jingyang handles investor contact. Hometown-name detail is from Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou_Changchuan_Technology).

name: John Catsimatidis
current_role: Owner, Chairman and CEO, Red Apple Group (Gristedes/D'Agostino, United Refining, WABC radio); director, Turning Point Brands
profile: Greek-born (Nisyros, 1948), Harlem-raised grocer who dropped out of NYU to buy into the store he clerked at, opened the first Red Apple in 1971 and later bought Gristedes. In 1986 he acquired Pennsylvania refiner United Refining (Warren, PA), now the core of his energy holdings, alongside NYC real estate. Since 2020 he has owned WABC radio, where he hosts 'The Cats Roundtable'.
interesting_fact: He hosts a weekly political talk-radio show, The Cats Roundtable, and bought the station that airs it (WABC 770 AM) in 2020; he ran for NYC mayor as a Republican in 2013.
deep_cut_fact: Before oil he dabbled in aviation: he invested in charter carrier Capitol Air in 1984 and in 1992 launched his own charter airline, Capitol Air Express, which flew from 1993 to 1996 in the old Capitol Air livery. He studied electrical engineering at NYU (Brooklyn Tech '66) before quitting 8 credits short.

public_contacts.value: The Cats Roundtable (WABC 770 AM) - linked from his official site

notes: Very media-friendly; hosts his own radio show and does many interviews, so a guest-swap/radio angle may work. Red Apple Group HQ is 800 Third Ave, NYC (no published press email found). Wrote a memoir, 'How Far Do You Want to Go?' (listed on his site).

name: Trevor Rees-Jones
current_role: Founder, Chief Oil & Gas (Dallas); co-founder of The Rees-Jones Foundation
profile: Dallas oil-and-gas bankruptcy lawyer (Thompson & Knight) who switched to investing in wells in 1984 and founded Chief Oil & Gas in 1994. Chief was an early Barnett Shale and Marcellus driller; he sold Barnett assets to Devon in 2006 and Chief's Marcellus business to Chesapeake in 2022, and remains active in oil, gas and mining ventures plus large North Texas philanthropy.
interesting_fact: By 2005 Chief Oil & Gas was the second-largest producer in the Barnett Shale, having drilled more than 250 wells, and its 2006 Barnett sale to Devon and Crosstex brought roughly $2.6 billion in cash.
deep_cut_fact: He earned Eagle Scout with Troop 70 in 1966, and the Circle Ten Council's Trevor Rees-Jones Scout Camp is named after him; his foundation also funded the Rees-Jones Foundation Leadership Veranda at the Boy Scouts' Summit Bechtel Reserve.
notes: Low public profile; rarely gives interviews but did several with Hart Energy and D CEO. Foundation emails were taken from search snippets of the official contact page (site blocked direct fetch) - re-verify before use. Also a Dartmouth trustee (2010-14) and TCU trustee.

name: Lin Shu-hong
current_role: Co-founder and President (總裁) of Chang Chun Group, Taiwan petrochemicals (stepped down as chairman end-2013)
profile: Lin Shu-hong (林書鴻, also Suhon Lin, b. 1928) co-founded Chang Chun Group in 1949 with classmates Tseng Shin-yi and M.K. Liao on about $100. It grew into one of Asia's largest private petrochemical groups (resins, chemicals, electronic materials) with plants in Taiwan, China and SE Asia. Though he left the chairmanship in 2013, in his mid-90s he still toured plants weekly.
interesting_fact: Called 'the Edison of petrochemicals': in the early days he ran 5-6 experiments a day to perfect a plywood adhesive that won over 60+ Taiwanese plywood makers and was even sold to the US military. He was elected to ITRI's first class of Fellows (2012) and won a National S&T contribution award (2016).
deep_cut_fact: At 94 he still visited the Hsinchu, Miaoli, Mailiao, Changhua and Kaohsiung plants every week, read nightly before bed, and recommended Kazuo Inamori's book on work, which he had covered in sticky tabs and notes.
notes: Born 1 Aug 1928 (age ~98); Forbes 2026 still lists him and no death report found, but confirm before outreach. Famously low-profile; group is private with no press/IR desk found (website behind Cloudflare). Any approach would go via Chang Chun Group corporate office in Taipei.

name: Carlos Bulgheroni
current_role: Deceased (died 3 September 2016, aged 71, in the United States)
profile: Argentine oil and gas magnate who, with brother Alejandro, built Bridas (founded by their father) into Argentina's leading private energy group, later partnering with BP and CNOOC in Pan American Energy. He died of cancer in September 2016; Alejandro now leads the family business.
notes: Deceased: died 3 Sep 2016 (sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Bulgheroni ; https://www.pagina12.com.ar/diario/economia/2-308544-2016-09-04.html). Wealth was shared with brother Alejandro Bulgheroni (alive, chairman of Pan American Energy Group) - he would be the relevant outreach target instead.

name: Liu Hanyuan
current_role: Chairman, Tongwei Group; NPC deputy and vice chairman of the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce
profile: Liu left a job at the Meishan county hydropower bureau in Sichuan to build a fish-feed business (founded 1986) that became Tongwei Group, a global leader in aquafeed. Tongwei later moved into polysilicon and solar cells, becoming one of the world's largest PV manufacturers. He is a prominent lawmaker-advocate for solar and renewable-energy policy.
interesting_fact: Tongwei ranks among the world's largest players in two unrelated industries at once: aquaculture feed and solar (polysilicon/cells). Liu regularly files NPC/CPPCC proposals pushing PV, e.g. solar to cut smog and tax cuts for the PV industry.
deep_cut_fact: In spring 1983, aged ~18, he pooled 200 yuan savings plus money from his parents selling two pigs (500 yuan total) to build a 64 m2 submerged fish cage in a Meishan canal; stocking 185 kg of carp yielded 1,390 kg by autumn, reportedly a Sichuan record for fish yield per unit area.
notes: ir_email is the published board-secretary (Yan Ke) contact of listed Tongwei Co. (600438) per its 2024 annual report summary; Tongwei's English site publishes many news items about Liu's policy proposals, a good angle for an energy podcast.

name: Gordon Getty
current_role: Composer and philanthropist (Gordon P. Getty Family Foundation); Getty Oil heir
profile: Son of oil tycoon J. Paul Getty, he led the 1984 sale of Getty Oil to Texaco for $10.1B and in 1985 split the family trust into separate trusts. Now in his 90s, he is a working classical composer (operas Plump Jack, Usher House, The Canterville Ghost, Goodbye, Mr. Chips) and a major San Francisco arts donor; he co-founded PlumpJack Winery with Gavin Newsom in 1995.
interesting_fact: He has given more than $450 million to his philanthropic foundation since 2008, and New Century Chamber Orchestra dedicated its entire 2025-26 season in his honor; he was one of ten inaugural inductees into Opera America's Opera Hall of Fame (2020).
deep_cut_fact: An English-literature graduate of the University of San Francisco and longtime poet, he writes his own librettos; his most-performed vocal work is The White Election (1981), a cycle setting 31 Emily Dickinson poems for soprano and piano, performed at Lincoln Center and the Hermitage Theatre.

public_contacts.value: Nancy Shear Arts Services - sheararts@gmail.com (PR/press for his music only)
mail@rorkmusic.com (Rork Music, his publisher; music inquiries only)

notes: Born 1933; very old and private on business matters. Only published routes are music-related (publisher Rork Music, PR via Nancy Shear Arts Services); his site says funding requests are discarded. An energy-angle pitch is a stretch; an arts/legacy framing fits better. Wikipedia notes 2026-released documents showing past Epstein correspondence - sensitive topic.

name: Li Min
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Rockchip Electronics Co., Ltd. (SSE: 603893), Fuzhou
profile: Li Min cofounded Rockchip in Fuzhou in 2001 with Huang Xu and remains chairman (reappointed general manager in Jan 2025). Rockchip designs SoCs for AIoT devices, tablets and edge-AI products and listed in Shanghai in 2020; Li holds roughly 37% of the company, the source of his fortune.
interesting_fact: Rockchip, a Fuzhou chip designer, counts Intel, Samsung and Google among its customers and focuses on intelligent IoT and edge-AI processors.
deep_cut_fact: In December 2025 he donated 175,000 Rockchip shares (worth roughly RMB 31M at the time) to the education foundation of his alma mater, Fuzhou No. 1 Middle School (福州一中), 'to give back to his alma mater'.
notes: Low media profile; English name in Chinese is 励民. Best route is via Rockchip's securities/IR department. Some unofficial sites say he was born 1965 and graduated Zhejiang University 1991 - not verified.

name: Steven Hao
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Cognition (maker of the Devin AI software-engineering agent)
profile: MIT-trained competitive programmer and former early engineer at Scale AI who co-founded Cognition in late 2023 with Scott Wu and Walden Yan. Cognition's Devin autonomous coding agent (and its 2025 acquisition of Windsurf) drove rapid valuation jumps, making Hao a billionaire per Forbes.
interesting_fact: All three Cognition co-founders were International Olympiad in Informatics competitors; Forbes reported that the company's rapid growth made CTO Hao a billionaire within about two years of founding.
deep_cut_fact: At IOI 2014 in Taipei he placed 6th in the world for the United States, scoring perfect 100s on five of six problems (525/600) to win a gold medal.
notes: No published press email found; only company social accounts. CEO Scott Wu is the usual public face; Hao is the technical lead and appears at engineering conferences (e.g. GitNation speaker profile), a possible route.

name: Fan Hongwei
current_role: Chairman, Hengli Petrochemical Co. (SSE: 600346); Vice Chairman, Hengli Group
profile: Born 1967 in Wujiang, Suzhou, Fan co-founded what became Hengli Group with her husband Chen Jianhua, starting in textiles in 1994 and integrating upstream into polyester, PTA and a giant refinery-petrochemical complex on Changxing Island, Dalian. She chairs listed Hengli Petrochemical; Hengli Group posted 2024 revenue of RMB 871.5bn (Fortune Global 500 #81).
interesting_fact: Hengli's integrated 'from a drop of oil to a bolt of cloth' chain helped break foreign dominance of PX and PTA feedstocks in China; in July 2025 Fan was one of 100 private entrepreneurs given a national 'outstanding builder' award in Beijing.
deep_cut_fact: Hengli began in 1994 as the Wujiang Chemical Fiber Weaving Factory in Shengze, Suzhou, with just 27 employees; when Hengli Group was formally set up in 2003, Fan became its general manager running production and operations.
notes: hlzq@hengli.com is Hengli Petrochemical's board-office/investor mailbox (listed in 2025 and 2026 earnings-call notices); Chinese-language approach advisable. Very low international media profile.

name: Carlos
profile: Carlos Alberto Bulgheroni (1945-2016), Argentine co-owner (with brother Alejandro) of the family energy group Bridas, died on 3 September 2016. Record matched via source of wealth Bridas and shared_with Alejandro Bulgheroni.
notes: DECEASED 3 Sep 2016 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Bulgheroni). Name field is truncated ('Carlos'); country listed as Spain is wrong - he was Argentine. For Bridas/Pan American Energy, the living family principal is his brother Alejandro Bulgheroni.

name: Romesh Wadhwani
current_role: Founder & Chairman, SAIGroup (SymphonyAI, ConcertAI); Founder & Chairman, Wadhwani Foundation
profile: Born in Karachi in 1947 and educated at IIT Bombay and Carnegie Mellon (PhD), Wadhwani made his fortune founding Aspect Development and later ran software PE firm Symphony Technology Group. He now heads SAIGroup, which includes SymphonyAI (backed by his $1B commitment) and ConcertAI. His Wadhwani Foundation funds entrepreneurship and AI-for-good work in India.
interesting_fact: Aspect Development, which he founded in 1991, was acquired by i2 Technologies in 1999 for $9.3 billion in stock. In 2020 India awarded him the Padma Shri.
deep_cut_fact: Before Aspect, he spent a decade running two startups. One was American Robot Corporation, which made computer-integrated manufacturing software. The other was Compu-Guard Corporation, an early technology-enabled energy-management company.

public_contacts.value: Chris Gale (Gale Strategies), SymphonyAI media contact: Chris@GaleStrategies.com

notes: The Compu-Guard energy-management startup is a natural hook for an energy-focused podcast. He also sits on the boards of trustees of CSIS and the Kennedy Center. The best route is SymphonyAI's PR contact.

name: Paul Foster
current_role: Founder & CEO, Franklin Mountain Investments (El Paso, TX); former founder/chairman of Western Refining
profile: A Baylor-trained CPA who kept the books for small Southwest refineries, Foster took over bankrupt El Paso Refining with partners in 1992, built Western Refining and sold it to Tesoro in 2017 ($6.4B deal). Via Franklin Mountain Investments he holds 30+ businesses (real estate, restaurants, sports); in 2025 he sold Franklin Mountain Energy for about $2.5B.
interesting_fact: He is part owner of the El Paso Chihuahuas Triple-A baseball team (via MountainStar Sports Group) and in 2007 gave $50M to help create the Paul L. Foster School of Medicine at Texas Tech in El Paso.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Lovington, New Mexico (class of 1975), he earned an accounting degree from Baylor in 1979 and then started out working at the local refinery back in Lovington before moving to El Paso.
notes: Very relevant to energy angle: serves on the Dallas Fed Energy Advisory Council and was appointed by Gov. Abbott to the ERCOT board selection committee (https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-appoints-foster-to-ercot-board-selection-committee). Best route is Franklin Mountain Investments' general inbox.

name: Torbjorn Tornqvist
current_role: Former co-founder and CEO of Gunvor Group (oil trader, since renamed Centalion); stepped down Dec 2025 in a management buyout; head of Artemis Racing sailing team
profile: Stockholm-born (1953), Geneva-based oil trader who co-founded Gunvor in 1997 and grew it into one of the world's largest independent energy traders. He bought out co-founder Gennady Timchenko's stake in 2014. In Dec 2025 he resigned as CEO and agreed to sell his ~86% stake to ~60 senior employees, partly vendor-financed; the firm has since rebranded as Centalion.
interesting_fact: He founded the Artemis Racing sailing team in 2006, which reached the Louis Vuitton Cup final in the 2013 America's Cup challenger series and helped bring Sweden back into the America's Cup.
deep_cut_fact: He came to competitive sailing late: he started crewing with Russell Coutts at the Swan Worlds, Coutts 'talked me into a TP52', and they won the MedCup and the championship in the same season, after only about three years of sailing. He still helms his own RC44 on the 44Cup circuit.
notes: No personal or office contacts published. He has left Gunvor/Centalion, so company press office is no longer a route to him. Artemis Racing (sailing) is the only active public affiliation. Avoid Russia/Timchenko/US Treasury topics; they are the context of his exit.

name: Pyotr Aven
current_role: Co-founder/shareholder of LetterOne (L1) and Alfa Group; former chairman of Alfa-Bank (2011-2022); art collector based in Surrey, UK
profile: Moscow-born economist Pyotr (Petr) Aven was Russia's minister of foreign economic relations in 1992 before joining Alfa-Bank, which he ran as president (1994-2011) and chairman until 2022. With Mikhail Fridman and partners he co-owns Alfa Group and LetterOne. Sanctioned by the EU/UK in 2022, he stepped off LetterOne's board and now focuses on his art collection and writing.
interesting_fact: He owns what is described as the largest/best private collection of Russian art (Goncharova, Petrov-Vodkin, Chagall, Kandinsky), lent to Tate, the Royal Academy, MoMA and Fondation Louis Vuitton; in 2022 he bought a building in Riga for a planned private museum.
deep_cut_fact: His collecting began in childhood with stamps and toy cars; the first painting he bought was a 1920s still life by Pavel Kuznetsov. As a young economist he was seconded to IIASA in Laxenburg, Austria, and he has lectured at Moscow's Higher School of Economics since 2007.
notes: Under EU/UK/US sanctions since 2022 - check legal/editorial implications before any engagement. petraven.info describes itself as his website (email appears in its schema.org metadata); appears to be a reputation-style site, so treat accounts linked there with some caution. Books: 'The Age of Berezovsky', 'Gaidar's Revolution' (free at petr-aven-books.com).

name: Liu Debing
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director & Chairman, Knowledge Atlas Technology / Zhipu AI (Z.ai), HKEX: 2513
profile: Co-founder and chairman of Zhipu AI, the Beijing developer of the GLM large language models, spun out of Tsinghua University's knowledge-engineering lab (AMiner) in 2019. He handles fundraising and business decisions. Zhipu listed in Hong Kong in January 2026, billed as the world's first listed LLM company, raising about $560M, and in 2026 changed its English short name to Z.AI.
interesting_fact: Speaking to Bloomberg TV on the day Zhipu listed, Liu said the AI price war would go global: if Zhipu can keep its prices at about one-seventh of its rivals', international customers will have to accept it.
deep_cut_fact: Before Zhipu, Liu earned a computer science PhD at the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Institute of Computing Technology, then worked at Technicolor's China research institute before joining Tsinghua as a senior engineer. He was one of Zhipu's six founders.
notes: Zhipu is on the U.S. Entity List (added 2025). No dedicated IR or press email found in its HKEX filings; best route is the company website or its HK IR channel. Chinese-language outreach is advisable.

name: Cho Jyh-jer
current_role: Retired; former Vice Chairman of MediaTek (retired June 2015)
profile: MediaTek co-founding veteran who joined as president in 1997 when the chip designer was spun off from United Microelectronics (UMC), and was promoted to vice chairman in 2005 to focus on new products and strategy. He retired in June 2015; his wealth comes mainly from his MediaTek stake. No public role since retirement was found.
interesting_fact: One of the founding veterans who fought alongside MediaTek chairman Tsai Ming-kai from the company's optical-disc-drive chip days, before MediaTek became one of the world's top smartphone chip designers.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer from National Chiao Tung University (communication engineering), he came out of NCTU's famed 'Lab 307' under Prof. Wu Chung-yu, one of the first master's cohorts in a lab that produced many of Taiwan's IC-design leaders.
notes: Very private, retired since 2015; no published personal/office contact found. Deep-cut fact taken from search-indexed text of GVM/NYCU pages (gvm.com.tw not fetchable here) - double-check before use. Alive status not confirmed but no death report found; still on 2026 Forbes real-time list.

name: N. Murray Edwards
current_role: Executive Chairman, Canadian Natural Resources Ltd.; owner, Edco Financial Holdings; chairman/co-owner, Calgary Sports & Entertainment Corp. (Calgary Flames)
profile: Regina-born lawyer-turned-financier who built his fortune backing and running Canadian energy companies, above all oil-sands giant Canadian Natural Resources (executive chairman), plus Ensign Energy, Magellan Aerospace and Imperial Metals. He also leads the Calgary Flames ownership group and owns Resorts of the Canadian Rockies. He moved his residency from Calgary to London in 2016.
interesting_fact: In high school Edwards worked four nights a week as a hockey referee; he also worked on a garbage crew and had a summer job at a beer factory with unlimited beer on breaks.
deep_cut_fact: A keen investor as a student, Edwards rang the bell on Oct 3, 2002 to launch the 'N. Murray Edwards MarketWatch' stock-ticker board he donated to his alma mater's business school in Saskatoon, years before it was renamed the Edwards School of Business (2007).

notes: Very low public profile; rarely gives interviews. Best route is likely via Canadian Natural's investor relations or the Edwards School of Business (USask), where he sits on the Dean's Advisory Council. Lives primarily in London (UK) since 2016.
