interesting_fact: His collection of Egyptian antiquities is one of the largest still in private hands; his Fondation Gandur pour l'Art (est. 2010) is planning a museum in Caen, France, on a 51,000 m² site.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Alexandria, Egypt until age 12, studied law and political science at Lausanne and history at the Sorbonne, and started in 1976 at commodities trader Philipp Brothers (Phibro), spending eight years at its Zug subsidiary before founding AOG.
notes: Listed country UK but based in Geneva/Switzerland. info@fg-art.org is the general mailbox of his art foundation; Oryx Energies (AOG's African downstream energy arm, Geneva) is the business route. Hurun/Forbes listings stale since ~2016.

name: Alexander Knaster
current_role: Founder, Pamplona Capital Management (London); majority owner of Pisa SC; founder of The Mark Foundation for Cancer Research
profile: Moscow-born (1959) financier who emigrated to the US at 16, studied EE/maths at Carnegie Mellon and got a Harvard MBA, ran CSFB Russia and then Alfa-Bank (1998-2004) before founding Pamplona Capital in 2004, a London private-equity/TMT manager (~$15B AUM in 2021). He bought 75% of Italian club Pisa in 2021 (promoted to Serie A in 2025) and has put the bulk of his assets into The Mark Foundation for Cancer Research.
interesting_fact: He named Pamplona Capital after the San Fermin festival in Pamplona, which he attended after graduating from Harvard Business School.
deep_cut_fact: Energy roots: in 1980, fresh out of Carnegie Mellon, he took a job as an engineer with Schlumberger working on oil platforms in the Gulf of Mexico. He later endowed the Alexander M. Knaster Scholarship Fund (1993) for CMU electrical & computer engineering undergrads.

public_contacts.value: ed.orlebar@tbcardew.com (Tavistock/TB Cardew - media enquiries for Pamplona)
info@themarkfoundation.org (The Mark Foundation for Cancer Research)

notes: Wikipedia article flagged for possible COI editing; facts used are biographical basics. Political donor (UK Conservatives) - avoid. Pamplona has moved away from energy; his podcast hooks are the Schlumberger start, Alfa-Bank era and Pisa football. Best route: Pamplona media contact at TB Cardew.

name: Sanjay Singal
current_role: Former chairman & managing director / promoter, Bhushan Power & Steel Ltd (company now owned by JSW Steel)
profile: Sanjay Singal, from the family behind the Bhushan steel businesses, built Bhushan Power & Steel into a large integrated steelmaker with operations in Odisha. The company went into insolvency in 2017, and JSW Steel took it over through a resolution plan (₹19,700 crore). He no longer controls the business and has spent recent years contesting the process in court.
interesting_fact: In September 2025 the Supreme Court of India upheld JSW Steel's ₹19,700 crore resolution plan for Bhushan Power & Steel, after briefly ordering liquidation in May 2025 at the former promoters' urging.
notes: He is a low-value and sensitive outreach target: he lost control of BPSL in insolvency, faced ED/CBI fraud proceedings, and the Supreme Court criticised the former promoters in 2025. No published contacts or public profile were found. No positive, sourced deep-cut fact was found.

name: Lin Zhiqiang
current_role: Chairman, Sanan Optoelectronics Co. (SSE: 600703), Xiamen; director at Fujian Sanan Group
profile: Eldest son of Sanan Group founder Lin Xiucheng (Hurun lists the fortune jointly). Born 1974 in Anxi, Fujian, he joined the family group in 1996, became Sanan Optoelectronics' general manager in 2011 and chairman in July 2017. Sanan is China's largest LED chip maker and is expanding into SiC/GaN compound semiconductors for EVs, inverters and power electronics.
interesting_fact: Sanan reached the stock market via a 2008 backdoor listing into the suspended, loss-making Tianyi Technology, which was turned into China's LED chip leader after the family injected Sanan Electronics' LED wafer and chip assets.
deep_cut_fact: He studied economic management at the PLA Naval Command College and has served as a local people's congress deputy in Anxi County and in Xiamen's Siming District.
notes: IR email is the board-secretary contact in Sanan's 2025 annual report summary. Sensitive timing: in 2026 Sanan disclosed that founder Lin Xiucheng and vice-chairman Lin Kechuang were placed under investigation, and the company swung to losses. Deep-cut source is a secondary Chinese profile site; verify before use.

name: John B Hess
current_role: Director, Chevron Corp (since July 2025, after Chevron's $53B acquisition of Hess Corp); director, Goldman Sachs
profile: Son of Hess founder Leon Hess, he joined the family firm as a trainee in 1976 and was CEO from 1995 until 2025, turning Hess into an exploration-and-production company with a stake in Guyana's giant Stabroek oil discoveries and the Bakken. Chevron bought Hess for ~$53B (closed July 18, 2025) and he joined Chevron's board and its Public Policy & Sustainability Committee.
interesting_fact: Hess's 30% stake in Guyana's Stabroek block, one of the biggest oil finds of the past decade, was the main prize in Chevron's $53B takeover, which was delayed over a year by an arbitration with ExxonMobil.
deep_cut_fact: Despite growing up wealthy he pumped gas at the family's Hess stations, joined his father on foreign oil fields at age seven, and as a Harvard undergraduate studied in Beirut, becoming fluent in Arabic and Farsi.
notes: No personal or family-office contact published; Hess Corp no longer exists as a separate company, so Chevron (board) is the institutional route. Recent CEO talks frame oil and gas as needed alongside AI-driven power demand, a good podcast hook.

name: Thomas Kurian
current_role: CEO, Google Cloud (Alphabet), since January 2019
profile: Kerala-born, Princeton-trained engineer Thomas Kurian spent 22 years at Oracle, rising to president of product development over a ~35,000-person engineering org, which made him wealthy via Oracle equity. Since 2019 he has run Google Cloud, turning it into a profitable, fast-growing business at the centre of Google's AI infrastructure and data-center buildout.
interesting_fact: His identical twin George Kurian is CEO of NetApp; in 1996 the twins effectively swapped careers - George moved from Oracle to McKinsey while Thomas left McKinsey to join Oracle.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Pampady, Kottayam, he and his twin boarded at Jesuit-run St Joseph's Boys' High School in Bangalore; both got into IIT Madras but took the SAT there and won partial scholarships to Princeton, moving to the US at 17. He graduated summa cum laude in electrical engineering.
notes: Wealth listed by Hurun is attributed to Oracle; he now runs Google Cloud - highly relevant for a data-center/AI podcast. Route via Google Cloud press team. X handle @ThomasOrTK ('CEO of @GoogleCloud') confirmed only via an aggregator; he is also active on LinkedIn.

name: Mahabir Prasad Agarwal
current_role: Chairman Emeritus (advisory), Shyam Metalics and Energy Ltd (NSE: SHYAMMETL); stepped down as chairman in May 2025
profile: Kolkata-based first-generation steel entrepreneur and co-promoter of Shyam Metalics and Energy, an integrated maker of ferro alloys, steel, aluminium foil and captive power, listed in 2021. He chaired the company until May 2025, when he resigned citing his age. Brij Bhushan Agarwal became chairman and MD, and Mahabir Prasad Agarwal stayed on as chairman emeritus.
interesting_fact: When he stepped down as chairman in May 2025, Shyam Metalics kept him on as chairman emeritus in an advisory role rather than letting him retire outright.
notes: Elderly and retired from the chair, so a low public profile. The company's Head of IR is Pankaj Harlalka, per the Nov 2026 earnings-call transcript. Unverified social posts say he started as a steel trader around 1970 and opened a sponge-iron plant in Sambalpur in 1990; these are not used as facts. The current chairman and MD, Brij Bhushan Agarwal, is the more active spokesman.

name: Stefan Fuchs
current_role: CEO (Chairman of the Executive Board), FUCHS SE, Mannheim (contract extended to June 2029)
profile: Third-generation family leader of FUCHS (formerly Fuchs Petrolub), founded in 1931 in Mannheim and now the world's largest independent lubricants supplier with ~6,000 staff in 50+ countries. He joined in 1996, entered the Executive Board in 1999 and has been CEO since 2004; the board extended his contract in Oct 2025 to 2029. (Input name 'Stefan Fuch' is a misspelling.)
interesting_fact: FUCHS has grown from a 1931 Mannheim family business into the world's largest independent supplier of lubrication solutions, independent of the oil majors; Stefan Fuchs has run it for more than 20 years.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family firm he spent two years as an auditing assistant at Wollert-Elmendorff Deutsche Industrie-Treuhand in Mannheim, then was posted (1997-99) to Fuchs Lubricants Co. in Harvey, Illinois, responsible for Argentina, Brazil and Mexico. He also sits on the supervisory board of machine-tool maker TRUMPF.
notes: Input name misspelled ('Stefan Fuch'). Press contact Tina Vogel (FUCHS SE Public Relations) per July 2026 release. Born 1968; Mannheim University business graduate.

name: W Brett Welson
current_role: Chairman, Prairie Merchant Corporation (private merchant bank); co-founder (ret.) of FirstEnergy Capital
profile: W. Brett Wilson (input spelling 'Welson' is a typo) is a Saskatchewan-born investment banker who co-founded Calgary energy investment bank FirstEnergy Capital in 1993 (with Murray Edwards and others) and chaired it until 2008. He was a Dragons' Den panellist (seasons 3-5) and now invests via Prairie Merchant in energy, real estate, agriculture and sports (incl. a Nashville Predators stake).
interesting_fact: He bills himself as the all-time lead deal-making 'dragon' on CBC's Dragons' Den, and wrote the 2012 Penguin book 'Redefining Success: Still Making Mistakes'.
deep_cut_fact: Before finance, Wilson earned a civil engineering degree and spent three years working the oilfields of Western Canada for Imperial Oil, then did an MBA in entrepreneurship at the University of Calgary (1985) and started at McLeod Young Weir.
notes: Hurun $2B figure looks inflated (other estimates far lower). Very active and outspoken on social media; has had public controversies over posts (2018, 2020) - be aware. Prolific philanthropist (prostate cancer, domestic-abuse research, mental health) and regular podcast guest, so likely receptive.

name: Ronald Mc Aulay
current_role: Director, Sir Elly Kadoorie & Sons Ltd (Kadoorie family office); former long-time director of CLP Holdings and Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels
profile: Ronald McAulay (b. 1935/36), a Scottish-born Hong Kong businessman, married into the Kadoorie family. His wealth stems mainly from a roughly 10% stake, held through trusts, in CLP Holdings, Hong Kong's biggest power utility. He sat on CLP's board 1968-2016 and on Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels' board 1972-c.2017.
interesting_fact: He joined the board of CLP, Hong Kong's main power utility, in 1968 at age 32 and served nearly half a century, leaving on 1 October 2016.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the Kadoorie businesses he trained as an accountant: he is a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Scotland, holds a master's degree from the University of Glasgow, and was schooled at Gordonstoun.
notes: Very private and about 90 years old. I found no death report, and Wikipedia (edited 2026) lists him as living. No published personal contact; the only route is via the Kadoorie family office (Sir Elly Kadoorie & Sons, Hong Kong) or CLP corporate communications. Input lists the country as China (Hong Kong); he is a British citizen.

name: Catherine Lozinck
profile: Catherine Lozick (correct spelling), daughter of Swagelok co-founder Fred A. Lennon, inherited a majority stake in the Solon, Ohio valve and fittings maker. Forbes reports she died in January 2025 at age 79. Swagelok is now led by Fred Lennon's grandson Thomas F. Lozick as chairman and CEO.
notes: Deceased January 2025 per Forbes profile (https://www.forbes.com/profile/catherine-lozick/). Input name is misspelled ('Lozinck'). Family remains very private; Swagelok is run by Thomas F. Lozick (https://swagelok.com/en/about/news/swagelok-announces-election-of-directors).

name: Maria del Carmen Sundblad Beccar Varela
current_role: Matriarch and shareholder of the Perez Companc Family Group (Argentina); founder of Munchi's ice cream and driving force behind Temaikèn.
profile: Born 1942, 'Munchi' Sundblad is the widow of Gregorio Pérez Companc (d. 2024), whose family controls Pecom (oil & gas services/production, expanding in Argentine upstream), Molinos Río de la Plata food and farmland. She built her own businesses: the Munchi's ice-cream chain, a Jersey dairy herd, and the Temaikèn bioparque in Escobar.
interesting_fact: She personally decided to build Temaikèn in Escobar, which opened in 2002 as Latin America's largest theme/bioparque, and she weighed in on the family's historic 2002 sale of Pecom Energía to Petrobras for about US$1bn.
deep_cut_fact: Her ice-cream brand Munchi's is named after her own childhood nickname; she also raises prize Jersey cattle at the family's San Isidro Labrador cabaña in Escobar, which she visited weekly, and La Nación wrote she only raises her voice when her bulls win at a rural show.
notes: Extremely private family ('extremists of anonymity'); no personal channels. Alive status presumed (on Hurun Global 2025-26 lists, no obituary found; would be 84). Contacts are company forms only (Munchi's, Pecom). Husband Gregorio died June 2024.

name: Giannis Vardinogiannis
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Motor Oil (Hellas) Corinth Refineries; Chairman & CEO, Avin Oil
profile: Eldest son of the late Vardis Vardinoyannis and head of the Vardinoyannis group, which controls Greek refiner Motor Oil Hellas. CEO since 2021 and chairman since Nov 2024, he has pushed the refiner into renewables (2.2 GW via the 2024 Anemos RES deal), waste/circular economy and banking (Optima Bank, listed 2023), with interests in shipping, upstream and hospitality.
interesting_fact: He ran Panathinaikos FC from 2000, taking the club to the Champions League quarter-finals in 2001-02, and was a founding member and later president of Greece's Super League.
deep_cut_fact: A Vassar economics graduate, he won the Greek Rally championship six straight times (1987-1992) in a Lancia Delta with co-driver Kostas Stefanis, and in 2024 founded the private team Cyclon Rally Sport.
notes: Also spelled Yannis/Ioannis Vardinoyannis. No published personal or press email verified (moh.gr blocked automated access); Motor Oil IR officer listed as Mary Psyllaki on market-data sites.

name: Robin Khuda
current_role: Founder and CEO, AirTrunk
profile: Dhaka-born accountant who moved to Sydney at 18, worked at Fujitsu, PIPE Networks and NEXTDC (as CFO), then founded hyperscale data-center operator AirTrunk in 2015. Blackstone and CPP Investments bought AirTrunk in 2024 in a A$24B (~US$16B) deal; he remains CEO and is expanding across APAC, the Middle East and India (a ~US$30B India plan announced in 2026).
interesting_fact: In AirTrunk's early days he dipped into his retirement savings to keep it afloat and came close to bankruptcy; in 2024 he was named AFR Business Person of the Year. In 2025 he gave A$100M to the University of Sydney for a 20-year women-in-STEM program.
deep_cut_fact: Right before founding AirTrunk he left NEXTDC to become CEO of Mint Wireless, a telecom payments company; he says he had been watching the cloud boom since 2010-11 and planning his own data-center business.
notes: Elected Fellow of ATSE in 2026. Runs the Khuda Family Foundation (women in tech, mental health). Also founded luxury developer Ondas. Excellent fit for the data-center podcast; route via AirTrunk media.

name: Amjad Masad
current_role: Cofounder and CEO, Replit
profile: Jordan-raised son of refugees who moved to the US in 2012 as an early engineer at Codecademy, then worked on Facebook's JavaScript infrastructure before cofounding Replit in 2016 with his wife Haya Odeh. Replit became a leader in AI 'vibe coding' agents and was valued at $9bn after a $400m round in March 2026.
interesting_fact: As a teenager in Jordan he made money building software management systems for local internet cafes; Replit's backers now include a16z, Coatue, Shaquille O'Neal, Jared Leto and Qatar's QIA.
deep_cut_fact: Before Replit he was tech lead on Facebook's JavaScript infrastructure team, which built or maintained the Babel compiler, Jest and the React Native packager; before that he was Codecademy's #1 employee, briefly at Yahoo, and worked in cybersecurity while in college.
notes: Very active and accessible on X (@amasad); has done many podcasts, so a direct X reply/DM plus press@replit.com is the best route. Strong AI/data-center angle (compute-hungry coding agents).

name: Zhu Gongshan
current_role: Founder, chairman and joint CEO of GCL Technology Holdings (3800.HK); chairman of GCL Group (Golden Concord)
profile: Born 1958 in Funing, Yancheng, Jiangsu, Zhu founded GCL in Hong Kong in 1990, first building cogeneration power plants, then moving into solar-grade polysilicon from 2006. GCL Tech became one of the world's largest polysilicon makers and is now pushing low-energy FBR granular silicon. He also chairs the Asian Photovoltaic Industry Association and the Global Green Energy Industry Council.
interesting_fact: Zhu trained as a power engineer, graduating from Nanjing Electric Power College (now Nanjing Institute of Technology) in 1981. GCL's first business was thermal and cogeneration power plants, years before it became a solar-materials giant.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding GCL he worked ordinary jobs from 1978, including as a shop sales clerk. He later chaired the SNEC Hydrogen Energy Industry Alliance Council and was named one of the 'Ten Outstanding Contributors to New China's New Energy Industry' in its 70th year.
notes: ESG@gcl-power.com is the corporate contact printed in GCL Tech's 2025 annual/ESG report (Suzhou HQ, tel +86 512 6853 3900); no dedicated press email was found. He speaks often at SNEC and global solar forums, so a conference is a plausible route. The sales-clerk detail comes from an ifeng profile (https://finance.ifeng.com/people/comchief/zhugongshan.shtml); the award and hydrogen role from the HKEX annual report.

name: William Koch
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Oxbow Corporation / Oxbow Carbon (West Palm Beach, Florida)
profile: William 'Bill' Koch, one of the four sons of Koch Industries co-founder Fred Koch, founded Oxbow in 1983 after leaving the family business; it grew into a major trader and processor of petroleum coke, coal, sulphur and other carbon products. He remains chairman, and is also a big collector of art, wine and Old West memorabilia.
interesting_fact: He won the 1992 America's Cup with his America3 syndicate, then in 1995 entered 'Mighty Mary', a boat crewed mostly by women, in the next Cup.
deep_cut_fact: In June 2011 he paid about $2.3m at Brian Lebel's Old West auction in Denver for the 'Upham tintype', the only authenticated photo of Billy the Kid; it joined his Wild West collection that includes Custer's rifle and Remington bronzes.
notes: Born 1940; listed on Forbes real-time 2026, no death reports found. Oxbow is private; a 2015 Oxbow press release listed a Corporate Communications Office in West Palm Beach (phone 561-907-5422, Director Corporate Affairs Brad Goldstein) - may be outdated. oxbow.com did not respond to direct fetch. Avoid the Koch-brothers feud and Oxbow litigation topics.

name: Mariarosa Lavelli
current_role: Major shareholder (~11%) of Technoprobe S.p.A. (Euronext Milan); co-founder of the Fondazione Mariarosa e Giuseppe Crippa
profile: Widow of Giuseppe Crippa (d. July 2025), an ex-STMicroelectronics engineer who founded Technoprobe, now a global leader in probe cards for chip testing used by Nvidia, Apple, TSMC and others. She handled the administration from the start and was still reported in 2022 to follow the family company's accounts. Owns ~11% since the 2022 IPO.
interesting_fact: Technoprobe started in the garage and attic of the Crippa family home in Merate (Lecco). In 1993 the nucleus was Giuseppe, son Cristiano, Mariarosa on administration and two employees. It moved to its first building in 1996 with about 10 staff.
deep_cut_fact: In May 2023 she and Giuseppe set up the Fondazione Mariarosa e Giuseppe Crippa to give structure to the family's and Technoprobe's philanthropy. Il Giorno noted she 'still follows the accounts' of the family firm even after it made Giuseppe a billionaire at 87.
notes: Recently widowed (July 2025), so be sensitive. Never gives interviews; route via Technoprobe press office. The family (son Cristiano Crippa, CEO Stefano Felici) is the public face. The foundation's start date is given as May 2023 in Technoprobe materials.

name: Li Jianli (励建立)
current_role: Chairman, Shenzhen Kedali Industry Co. (科达利, SZSE 002850)
profile: Ningbo-born mould designer who co-founded Kedali in Shenzhen in 1996 with his brother using ~RMB 20,000 of savings. Kedali moved from stamping dies to phone-battery parts and, from 2007, to precision structural parts for EV batteries; it listed in Shenzhen in 2017 and supplies CATL, BYD, CALB, EVE, Panasonic and LG, with ~32% global share in 2023.
interesting_fact: In 2007, as iPhone-era pouch cells threatened his phone-battery parts business, he put more than half its profits into EV battery structural parts; R&D succeeded by 2010 and the segment grew from RMB 66m revenue (2013) to RMB 930m (2016).
deep_cut_fact: He studied mould design at a technical secondary school, graduated in 1991 and went to Shenzhen as a die designer at a Hong Kong-owned firm. Kedali's break came in 1999 when BYD asked it to co-develop phone-battery parts: after 20+ attempts in a year it matched Japanese imports at about a third of the price.
notes: Low media profile; Chinese-language outreach advisable. No published email found on company site; best route is Kedali's investor-interaction page (cninfo IRM, linked from its website) or the company contact page https://www.kedali.com.cn/contact.html. Brother Li Jianju (励建炬) is president.

name: Airat Shaimiev
current_role: Head (CEO) of JSC Tatavtodor, Tatarstan's state road-construction company; co-owner of TAIF shareholders' stake in Sibur
profile: Son of Tatarstan's first president, Mintimer Shaimiev. He built his fortune as a co-owner of TAIF Group, a Tatarstan holding with refining and petrochemical assets that merged into Sibur in 2021; TAIF shareholders received 15% of Sibur. He still runs Tatavtodor, the regional road builder, which reported 2025 contracts worth billions of rubles.
interesting_fact: With his brother Radik and his son Timur he also owns MNKT, a small oil producer in Tatarstan (per Forbes).
deep_cut_fact: He practiced karate in Soviet times, when the sport was banned in the USSR. After it was legalised he won the Kazan championship, then took up motor racing; he and his brother raced in the first events at the Vysokaya Gora autodrome in 1996.
notes: He is under UK sanctions (OpenSanctions entry gb-hmt-15608), so outreach may raise compliance and reputational issues. The only published contact is Tatavtodor's general company email. He gives few interviews.

name: Huo Qinghua
current_role: Founder and chairman, China Kingho Energy Group (中国庆华能源集团) / Inner Mongolia Qinghua Group (last reported)
profile: Huo Qinghua (霍庆华) built China Kingho (Qinghua) Group, once called China's largest private coal miner, from a 1996 start in Alashan, Inner Mongolia, expanding into coal chemicals, logistics and overseas projects (assets RMB 68.6B in 2014). He was on Forbes' billionaire list 2013-2018, but the group struggled after the coal downturn.
interesting_fact: In 2011 Kingho announced plans to build a coal terminal at Mozambique's Beira port and upgrade the Sena railway to the Moatize coal mines, and had proposed a $19B coal development in Pakistan's Thar field.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming a coal magnate he served in the army and then worked as a physician at the hospital of Ningxia's Shitanjing Mining Bureau, studying economic management at the Ningxia Coal Workers' University.
notes: No recent (post-2018) news on him found; no death reports found. Per NBD (2018) the group fell into financial distress after 2013 with creditor lawsuits and court enforcement lists, so approach with care; likely not a current billionaire. No published personal/press contacts.

name: Evangelos Mytilineos
current_role: Chairman and CEO, METLEN Energy & Metals (Athens/London-listed)
profile: Greek industrialist (b. 1954, Athens) who in 1990 founded the modern Mytilineos group from his grandfather's 1908 metallurgy business, listed it in Athens in 1995, renamed it METLEN in 2024 and added a London listing in 2025. METLEN runs aluminium plants and bauxite mines, builds solar and storage projects worldwide and is Greece's largest independent electricity supplier.
interesting_fact: METLEN's roots go back to a metallurgy business founded in 1908 by his grandfather, also named Evangelos; he turned it into one of Greece's largest industrial and energy groups and moved its primary listing to London in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: A Moraitis School alumnus, he holds an economics BSc from the University of Athens and an MSc from the London School of Economics; the University of Piraeus gave him an honorary doctorate in 2019, and his family hails from Koroni in the Peloponnese.
notes: No personal social media found. Route via METLEN media/contact-us page (info@metlen.com). Strong energy fit: solar/storage EPC, power supply and energy-intensive aluminium. Deep-cut fact is light (from Wikipedia); my web-search quota ran out before I could look further.

name: Farkhad Akhmedov
current_role: Private investor; chairman/shareholder of AZNAR (Azerbaijani natural-juice and agriculture company); former Russian senator
profile: Baku-born (1955) Azerbaijani-Russian businessman who started trading furs in London, founded Tansley Trading to supply equipment to Soviet gas producers, and built a stake in Siberian gas producer Northgas, selling his 49% to Novatek in 2012 for ~$1.4B. Sat in Russia's Federation Council 2004-2009. Now invests privately, incl. AZNAR juice and agriculture in Azerbaijan.
interesting_fact: He invested $55 million in a pomegranate juice factory in his native Azerbaijan, in the region where his father worked during the Soviet era.
deep_cut_fact: Before oil and gas, he served in the Soviet Navy (1975-77) as a senior sergeant and platoon commander, then earned a degree in the technology and merchandising of fur products from the Moscow Veterinary Academy (1983), the expertise behind his first business selling furs in London.
notes: Sensitive: under UK sanctions since April 2022 (EU lifted its sanctions in Sept 2023) and subject of a long, heavily covered divorce case; avoid both. He has also been the first ethnic Azerbaijani in Russia's upper house. No published personal/office contact found; web-search budget ran out before checking AZNAR's site.

name: Lu Feng
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Wind Information Co., Ltd. (万得信息, Shanghai)
profile: Lu Feng (陆风) founded Wind Information in Shanghai in the 1990s (sources give 1994 or 1998) and built it into mainland China's dominant financial-data terminal, often described as China's answer to Bloomberg, used by brokers, fund houses, banks and QFIIs. He remains chairman and is a part-time vice chair of the Shanghai Federation of Industry and Commerce's 14th executive committee.
interesting_fact: Wind's terminal is the default data source cited across Chinese financial media, research reports and academic papers; investors in the company have included Hillhouse Capital (2015) and Xinhu Zhongbao (2018).
deep_cut_fact: In a rare 2021 keynote at Huatai Securities' fintech open day he recalled that in 2006 Wind adopted the slogan '金融就是数据' ('finance is data'), described a 'digital twin enterprise' goal, and promoted Wind's 'Shared by Wind' program to share its data and networks with startups.
notes: Very low-profile founder; rarely gives interviews. Name collides with a Peking University economist Lu Feng (born 1951) - different person. Wealth is financial data, not energy, despite the 'energy' focus tag. Route via Wind corporate office in Shanghai.

profile: Hurun's 2026 China Rich List adds Zhu Mengqian (b. 1991, Wuhan; master's degree) jointly with her father Zhu Shuangquan, chairman of Wuhan-based Dinglong, a maker of semiconductor CMP polishing pads/slurries, display materials and printing consumables. name: Harvey Jones
current_role: Managing Partner, Square Wave Ventures; NVIDIA director since 1993 (Nvidia's board page lists him as Chair of the Board, plus audit and nominating/governance committees)
profile: EDA pioneer: co-founded Daisy Systems in 1981 (president/CEO to 1987), then led Synopsys 1987-1998 as CEO and executive chairman, and co-founded processor-IP firm Tensilica in 1997 (chairman until Cadence bought it in 2013). No personal social accounts or published Square Wave contact found; Nvidia corporate PR is the formal route. Chair title taken from nvidia.com board page (not independently re-verified).

name: Femi Otedola
current_role: Chairman and largest shareholder (~27.7% as of Aug 2026), First HoldCo Plc (parent of First Bank of Nigeria)
profile: Lagos businessman who built Zenon Petroleum into a dominant diesel supplier, later controlled Forte Oil and then Geregu Power, whose majority stake he sold in 2025 for about $750M. name: Pantas Sutardja
current_role: Director, Credo Technology Group (Nasdaq: CRDO); founder & CEO of LatticeWork.
profile: Indonesian-born engineer (UC Berkeley EE/CS PhD, ex-IBM Almaden) who cofounded Marvell in 1995 with his late brother Sehat and Weili Dai, serving as VP engineering and CTO until 2014. He backed Credo's 2015 Series A and sits on its board (~3% stake); Credo's high-speed connectivity chips/AECs are now a key AI data-center supplier. He also runs consumer-storage firm LatticeWork.

Designed for 180 Mb/s, it was already running near 240 Mb/s when Seagate asked for 240 - Seagate became Marvell's first customer. As boys in Singapore he and Sehat built a Van de Graaff generator from surplus copper wire.
notes: Strong data-center angle via Credo (AI interconnect). Credo contacts are company IR/media (published in FY2026 earnings release), not personal. Avoid Marvell 2016 accounting-probe ouster topic (concerned his brother/sister-in-law).

name: Igor Yusufov
current_role: Former Russian Minister of Energy (2001-04) and founder of Fund Energy; per Forbes Russia, no longer manages projects (since 2020) and divested declared assets by March 2022
profile: Dagestan-born (1956) power engineer turned official: ran the state reserves agency, served as Russia's energy minister 2001-04, then presidential envoy for international energy cooperation and a Gazprom board member (2003-13). After 2011 he invested via Fund Energy in oil and gas, mining and renewables, but Forbes Russia reports he exited those holdings by 2022.
interesting_fact: As energy minister he initiated the first Russian-American Business Energy Summit in Houston (Oct 2002), co-signing a joint statement with U.S. Energy Secretary Spencer Abraham and Commerce Secretary Donald Evans.
deep_cut_fact: Before government he was a working power engineer: after Novocherkassk Polytechnic he worked at Mosenergo, then spent four years in Cuba as a technology expert on the construction site of a Havana thermal power plant.
notes: Dropped off Forbes lists (listed as 'former'); says he has exited his assets. No published contact found; former company site corporationenergy.ru may be stale. Outreach to a former Russian minister may raise sanctions/compliance questions; check before contacting. Low fit unless covering Russian energy history.

name: Sanjay Mehrotra
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, Micron Technology (MU); director, CDW
profile: Kanpur-born (1958) electrical engineer (UC Berkeley BS/MS) who co-founded SanDisk in 1988 with Eli Harari and Jack Yuan and was its CEO 2011-2016 until the Western Digital sale. CEO of Micron since 2017, he has steered it into the AI boom via high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for data-center GPUs, which drove Micron's surge and his billionaire status.
interesting_fact: He holds dozens of flash-memory patents and was elected to the US National Academy of Engineering in 2022 for contributions to multilevel-cell (MLC) NAND flash design that made dense flash storage practical.
deep_cut_fact: Supporting himself from 18, his first job at Berkeley was collecting dirty dishes in the International House dining room - he quit after a few days to grade homework. Later, in 1984, he was slated to be one of four Atmel co-founders with mentor George Perlegos, but stayed at Seeq out of loyalty.
notes: Public-company CEO; requests go via Micron corporate communications. Very strong data-center/AI memory angle (HBM). Gave a 2019 Computer History Museum oral history, useful for prep.

name: Zhang Jianhui
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, HyperStrong (Beijing HyperStrong Technology / 海博思创, Shanghai STAR Market)
profile: Dr. Zhang Jianhui (张剑辉) founded HyperStrong in Beijing in 2011 after studying at Tsinghua and Berkeley and working as a chip R&D/design engineer in Silicon Valley. HyperStrong became one of China's top battery energy-storage system integrators (400+ projects, 70+ GWh in 30+ countries) and listed on the STAR Market in 2025. He now pushes a 'storage + X' strategy, including storage-plus-compute.
interesting_fact: In Sept 2026 HyperStrong broke ground in Baotou on an integrated storage-and-compute project with a 'token factory' (词元工厂): grid-side batteries co-sited with a distributed AI computing center selling metered AI compute, using its own solid-state transformer (HyperSST).
deep_cut_fact: Before energy storage he was a Silicon Valley chip R&D/design engineer ('from Tsinghua to Berkeley'); in Sept 2026 he was named one of the '2026 Beijing Role Models' (北京榜样) for August.
notes: Excellent fit for the energy x data-center theme (storage-compute 'token factory' in Baotou). HyperStrong has US offices (Chicago, Houston, San Francisco) and is shortlisted at the Energy Storage Awards in London on 19 Nov 2026, possible in-person angle. Contact is company-level only.

name: Feng Yongmao
current_role: Individual shareholder (5th largest, ~1.93% / 4.81M shares as of 30 Sep 2026) of Advanced Fiber Resources (Zhuhai), 300620.SZ; no board or management role
profile: Feng Yongmao (冯永茂) appears in AFR's filings only as a large private shareholder. AFR (光库科技), founded 2000 in Zhuhai and listed 2017, makes fiber-optic components and photonic chips (incl. thin-film lithium niobate modulators) for AI data centers, telecom, subsea cables and fiber lasers; it is controlled by state-owned Zhuhai Huafa. No public biography found.
interesting_fact: AFR is one of the few suppliers worldwide of core components for long-haul subsea optical networks, and now pitches its optical devices into AI data-center interconnects.
notes: Passive investor with no public profile; a 1.93% stake looks far below Hurun's ~$1.07B figure, so wealth attribution may rest on other holdings or be off. The IR email reaches the company, not him. Better AFR interviewees: co-chair/GM Wang Xinglong (ex-JDSU, Oplink), co-founder.

name: Farhad Ebrahimi
current_role: Private investor (Denver); former CEO and co-owner of Quark, Inc.; major holder of Royal Hawaiian Orchards and a First Solar investor
profile: Farhad 'Fred' Ebrahimi (87), an Iranian-born immigrant in Denver, joined desktop-publishing software maker Quark as CEO and co-owner in 1986 and later bought out co-founder Tim Gill; the family sold Quark to Platinum Equity in 2011. He then invested in Hawaii (owning ~80% of macadamia producer Royal Hawaiian Orchards by 2018) and in solar-panel maker First Solar.
interesting_fact: Quark was founded in Denver in 1981 with just $2,000; its QuarkXPress, launched in 1987 under Ebrahimi's leadership, reached roughly 90% of the desktop-publishing market by the late 1990s.
deep_cut_fact: He was not one of Quark's original 1981 founders (Tim Gill and Mark Pope) - he joined in 1986 as CEO and co-owner, bought Gill's entire stake in 2000, and is listed on Forbes' 2026 America's Richest Immigrants list.
notes: Very private; no personal site or published contact found. Do not confuse with his son Farhad Ebrahimi (climate philanthropist, Chorus Foundation) or the Iranian poet of the same name. Forbes: https://www.forbes.com/profile/farhad-ebrahimi/. Web-search budget ran out before checking Hawaii holdings/press routes.

name: Chi Fung Cheng
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Technology Officer and Director, Credo Technology Group (Nasdaq: CRDO)
profile: Chi Fung 'Lawrence' Cheng, 57, co-founded high-speed connectivity chipmaker Credo in 2008 after 11 years as an engineering director of analog design at Marvell, and has been CTO since. Credo's SerDes/DSP chips, retimers and 'ZeroFlap' active electrical cables connect servers and switches in AI data centers at up to 1.6T; it listed on Nasdaq in 2022. He holds roughly 4% of the company.
interesting_fact: Credo's active electrical cables (AECs) - copper cables with Credo DSPs built in - have become a key interconnect in AI clusters, with products spanning 32G to 200G per lane and 1.6T links.
deep_cut_fact: Before Marvell, Cheng spent 1994-1997 as a staff engineer at Actel Corporation, an FPGA/integrated-circuit maker, after earning an M.S. in electrical engineering at Purdue.
notes: Low-profile technical founder; CEO Bill Brennan is Credo's public face. IR contact is Dan O'Neil. Credo website blocked automated fetches (403), so no press email verified there.

name: Kirit Doshi
current_role: Minority shareholder (promoter-family member) of Waaree Energies Ltd, Mumbai
profile: Mumbai-based member of the Doshi family behind Waaree Energies, India's largest solar-module maker by capacity. Waaree began in 1990 under his brother Hitesh as a maker of thermal and pressure gauges for industrial boilers, moved into solar panels, and listed in October 2024 at a 70% premium to its IPO price; Kirit's minority stake made him a billionaire (Forbes, age 61).
interesting_fact: Waaree started out making thermal and pressure gauges for industrial boilers before becoming India's largest solar-module manufacturer, now with five module plants in India.
notes: Low-profile family shareholder; brother Hitesh Doshi (chairman) is Waaree's public face. Waaree's contact page lists the general company email waaree@waaree.com. Exact current executive title at Waaree not verified (web search budget exhausted); no deep-cut fact could be sourced.

name: Andrew Feldman
current_role: Co-founder, President and CEO, Cerebras Systems (Nasdaq: CBRS)
profile: Palo Alto-raised, Stanford BA/MBA serial founder who co-founded Cerebras in 2015-16 with his SeaMicro team to build the Wafer-Scale Engine, the largest chip ever made, for AI training and inference. Cerebras IPO'd on Nasdaq in May 2026 at $185/share, raising $5.55B and jumping ~68% on day one; he owns roughly 5% between stock and options.
interesting_fact: Cerebras' Wafer-Scale Engine uses an entire silicon wafer as one processor (WSE-3: 4 trillion transistors, 900,000 cores); in 2022 the Computer History Museum installed a permanent display of it as the first wafer-scale integration achieved in computing history.
deep_cut_fact: Data-center energy was his theme long before AI: his prior startup SeaMicro was 'founded to dramatically reduce the power consumed by servers' - its microservers used about a quarter of the power and a sixth of the space of conventional servers - and AMD bought it in 2012 for ~$334M.

public_contacts.value: pr@zmcommunications.com (ZM Communications, media contact on Cerebras press releases)

notes: Highly media-accessible and a frequent podcast guest; excellent fit for AI chips/inference and data-center power. PR agency contact dates from 2024 releases - check a recent Cerebras release for the current media contact. Personal X/LinkedIn not verified in this pass.

name: Wang Zhenggen
current_role: Director and General Manager, Suzhou Maxwell Technologies (迈为股份, SZSE: 300751)
profile: Wang Zhenggen (54) co-founded Suzhou Maxwell Technologies in 2010 with Zhou Jian; it listed in Shenzhen in 2018. Maxwell makes solar-cell production equipment (screen-printing, HJT and perovskite-silicon tandem lines) and has expanded into OLED/MicroLED laser tools and chip wafer-packaging equipment, selling into Thailand, Turkey and the US.
interesting_fact: Maxwell says it was the first company to localize complete solar-cell screen-printing lines and HJT cell lines in China, and its screen-printing lines have been No.1 by global market share every year 2018-2025; its tandem perovskite/silicon line targets >31% cell efficiency.
notes: Forbes profile: https://www.forbes.com/profile/wang-zhenggen/ (residence Suzhou). Co-founder Zhou Jian is chairman. Maxwell's IR site has an investor 'interactive platform' (SZSE Hudongyi) rather than a published IR email; the board-secretary email would be in its annual report. Semiconductor packaging tools give a chip/AI angle beyond solar.

name: Tang Xiaodong
current_role: Director and public-relations director, Bestechnic (BES, 恒玄科技), Shanghai (per 2020 IPO prospectus); co-controlling shareholder
profile: Tang Xiaodong (b. 1975, female) is one of Bestechnic's three co-controlling shareholders with her husband, chairman Liang Zhang, and vice chairman Zhao Guoguang. She co-funded its predecessor at the June 2015 founding and has been a director since 2019. Bestechnic makes low-power wireless SoCs for earbuds/wearables; STAR Market IPO Dec 2020.
interesting_fact: Bestechnic claims the world's first dual-mode Bluetooth earbud chip with integrated active noise cancellation (2016) and the first 28nm low-power Bluetooth audio chip (BES2300, 2018).
deep_cut_fact: Before chips she came from law: per Bestechnic's IPO prospectus she was a manager at international law firm O'Melveny & Myers (美迈斯律师事务所) from 2002 to 2009, and Bestechnic's predecessor was set up in 2015 by her, Zhao Guoguang and an investment vehicle.
notes: Hurun lists her (as 'Tang Xiaodong') jointly with Zhang Liang. Role is from the 2020 prospectus; confirm she is still a director in the latest annual report. As PR director she may be the natural route for media requests.

name: Jay Hyung Son
current_role: Co-founder and executive director, Innoscience (Suzhou) Technology (HKEX: 2577) - responsible for business development (per Dec 2024 prospectus)
profile: American semiconductor entrepreneur (age ~63) who co-founded Innoscience with chair Luo Weiwei; the two are its controlling shareholders. Innoscience is the world's largest GaN-dedicated chipmaker (8-inch GaN-on-silicon; ~30% global GaN power-device share in 2024), listed in Hong Kong in Dec 2024 and partnering with Nvidia on 800VDC power for AI data centers. He was GM of Inno Suzhou 2017-2023.
interesting_fact: In August 2025 Innoscience announced a collaboration with Nvidia on an 800-volt DC power architecture for AI data centers, and in December 2025 signed an MOU with Onsemi to accelerate GaN power device deployment.
deep_cut_fact: A 1987 UC Berkeley College of Engineering graduate, he ran earlier US-based R&D ventures before Innoscience - including serving as CEO of INNOEPI, Inc. and president of InnoScience Inc. (Delaware), both later wound down as the business moved to China.
notes: Very low public profile; the public face of Innoscience is chair Luo Weiwei (ex-NASA scientist). Role confirmed from Dec 2024 HKEX prospectus; current 2026 board status not re-verified (search budget exhausted). Strong AI data-center power (GaN/800VDC) angle.

name: Jin Xiaodong
current_role: Actual controller (controlling shareholder) of Anhui XDLK Microsystem (芯动联科, SSE STAR: 688582); not a current director or officer
profile: Jin Xiaodong (金晓冬) is the actual controller of XDLK, a Bengbu, Anhui maker of high-performance MEMS inertial sensors (gyroscopes, accelerometers) and pressure sensors. Founded in 2012, XDLK listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in June 2023; he controls it via vehicles such as MEMSLink Corp. plus a ~1.3% direct stake.
interesting_fact: XDLK aims to replace bulky traditional high-end inertial navigation hardware with chip-scale MEMS gyroscopes, and is pushing into autonomous driving and industrial robotics.
notes: Very low public profile; holds no executive title (chairman is Lü Dongfeng, GM/board secretary Lin Ming). Best route is via the company's board office/IR. Personal bio not verified; web-search budget ran out during this lane.

name: Rodney Lewis
current_role: Founder, President & CEO, Lewis Energy Group (San Antonio, Texas)
profile: Laredo-raised wildcatter (born 1954) who bought his first gas well in 1982 and launched Lewis Energy in 1983, building a large Eagle Ford shale position and becoming one of Texas' biggest private gas producers. In 2004 he became the first U.S. oilman contracted to drill for Pemex in Mexico. Still runs the privately held company; inducted into Hart Energy's Hall of Fame in 2023.
interesting_fact: He owns one of America's largest fleets of airworthy WWII fighters, including the P-38 'Glacier Girl' recovered from under a Greenland glacier, and founded the Lewis Air Legends collection in 2009; he has served on the National Air and Space Museum board.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a BA in criminal justice from what is now Texas A&M International University in Laredo, paid $13,000 for his first well, and in 2014 received Webb County's 'Angel of Hope' award for providing Christmas gifts to needy children.
notes: Goes by Rod Lewis. Private company; general info@ inbox is the only published email. Warbird aviation (Lewis Air Legends) is a strong rapport topic. No 2026 personal news found; alive status based on current company leadership listings.

name: Li Jun
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Leyard Optoelectronic Co. (SZSE: 300296), Beijing
profile: Economist-turned-entrepreneur who founded Leyard in Beijing in 1995 and built it into a leading LED/large-format display group (ChiNext IPO 2012), expanding via the 2015 acquisition of Oregon's Planar Systems and Germany's eyevis (2018), and into VR/AI-driven display and 'metaverse' tech. He was re-elected chairman and named general manager in February 2026.
interesting_fact: Before business, Li earned an economics doctorate at Renmin University and taught at the Central University of Finance & Economics (1987-1991). Leyard screens lit the 2008 Beijing Olympics opening ceremony and it supplied most of the giant LED floor for the 2022 Winter Olympics opening.
deep_cut_fact: For the 2008 Beijing Olympics opening ceremony Leyard made the displays that illuminated the Olympic Rings and a 1,300 m² 'Ground Bar' LED scroll tough enough to have cars driven across it.
notes: Profile assumes the Forbes 'Li Jun' (Leyard). The listed source of wealth 'Botheart' (Hurun unicorn record) could not be matched to Leyard and may belong to a different Li Jun (very common name) - identity marked uncertain for that reason. leyard2010@leyard.com is the board-secretary/IR mailbox (2026 filing).

name: Chen Gang
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Shanghai Aiko Solar Energy Co. (AIKO, SSE: 600732)
profile: Chen Gang founded Aiko Solar in 2009 (Guangdong Aiko Technology), a solar cell maker with plants in Foshan, Yiwu and Tianjin that sells globally. Aiko rose from a mid-sized player to the world's No.1 PERC cell shipper in 2018, listed via a backdoor deal with ST Xinmei in 2019, and now champions n-type back-contact (ABC) cells and modules. He continues to lead it through the industry's consolidation.
interesting_fact: Aiko went from outside China's top 10 cell makers to No.1 globally in PERC cell shipments in 2018; Chen chose a backdoor listing because 'in an industry reshuffle, time matters more than money.'
deep_cut_fact: In 2017, while ordinary mono cells were very profitable, he halted his own mono lines to bet on unproven tubular PERC tech, pre-agreeing with suppliers to convert the equipment back if it failed. His rule: 'If even the worst outcome isn't bad, you dare to do it' (最坏的结果都不坏，你就敢做了).
notes: Common name - matched via Aiko Solar. Gives interviews to Chinese press (People's Daily Energy, The Paper at SNEC 2025); likely needs Mandarin outreach. Co-owner listed: Ou Chunlian. No dedicated English IR email found; Chinese annual report may list a securities-affairs email.

name: Ou Chunlian
current_role: Co-holder (with Chen Gang) of the controlling family stake in Aiko Solar / Shanghai Aiko Solar Energy (爱旭股份, 600732.SH); no executive title found
profile: Hurun lists Ou Chunlian (欧春连) jointly with Chen Gang, founder, chairman and controller of Aiko Solar (爱旭股份), a leading Chinese maker of high-efficiency PV cells and modules. Chinese media say Chen Gang made the 2023 Hurun Global list 'with his wife', so she is probably his wife, but no public profile of her exists.
interesting_fact: Aiko was the first company to develop and mass-produce n-type ABC (all-back-contact) solar cells, which have no front-side electrodes. Chen Gang argues that the technology closest to the efficiency limit wins.
notes: No public information on Ou Chunlian herself. The realistic interviewee is Chen Gang (chairman, Aiko Solar), via company marketing/IR. A 2025 article says the SSE sent Aiko an inquiry letter about related-party transactions, so outreach may be sensitive.

name: Yao Junliang
current_role: Chairman of the board, Meijin Energy Group (controlling shareholder of Shanxi Meijin Energy, SZSE: 000723)
profile: Second-generation head of the Yao family's Shanxi coal-and-coke business, which began in 1981 under his father Yao Juhuo and grew into one of China's largest independent merchant coke and coal producers. Since 2017 he has pushed Meijin into hydrogen (production, storage, refuelling, fuel-cell vehicles), though coking still dominates revenue.
interesting_fact: Meijin's hydrogen push started in Guangdong: it helped create membrane-electrode maker Guangzhou Hongji Chuangneng, invested in fuel-cell firm Guohong Hydrogen, and in 2017 took control of Foshan Feichi (now Feichi Technology), a hydrogen fuel-cell bus and truck maker.
deep_cut_fact: The Yao family firm has its roots in 1981 Shanxi; in 1996 his father, then 65, gathered the family and said he was only a 'passing god of wealth' (guolu caishen) holding money that belonged to society before entrusting the business to the next generation.
notes: Listed arm Shanxi Meijin Energy (000723) is chaired by Yao Jinlong (CPPCC member); Chinese press calls Yao Junliang chairman of the Meijin group board. Company under financial strain in 2025-26 (rating cut, losses, pledged shares) - avoid wealth/debt topics. Hydrogen is the best hook; Chinese-language outreach advised.

name: Xia Feng
current_role: Co-founder and non-executive Director (since Oct 2008), Shanghai Bright Power Semiconductor (SSE STAR: 688368); director, Changsha Zuxing New Materials
profile: Xia Feng (夏风, b. ~1968) co-founded Shanghai Bright Power Semiconductor (晶丰明源) in 2008 with chairman Hu Liqiang; the fabless analog/mixed-signal chip designer makes LED-lighting driver, power-management and motor-control ICs. He holds ~19.6M shares directly and more via a partnership. Hurun also links his wealth to image-sensor maker GalaxyCore (格科微).
interesting_fact: When Bright Power was set up in Oct 2008 with just RMB 2 million of registered capital, Xia Feng put up 47% of it (RMB 940,000), almost as much as founder-CEO Hu Liqiang's 48.2%.
deep_cut_fact: Before chips, he started as a technician and assistant engineer at the Zhuzhou Zhongnan Radio Factory in Hunan, then became deputy head of the Zhuzhou zinc-oxide surge-arrester factory and later a VP at Shenzhen Zuxing Industrial (2025 annual report bio).

public_contacts.value: IR@bpsemi.com (Bright Power Semiconductor investor relations / board office)

notes: Non-executive, low-profile investor-director; no interviews found. GalaxyCore link is from Hurun and was not confirmed in filings checked. Route via Bright Power IR; chairman Hu Liqiang is the company's public face.

name: Ajay Puri
current_role: Executive Vice President, Worldwide Field Operations, NVIDIA (still listed with this title on an Aug 2026 SEC Form 4)
profile: Ajay 'Jay' Puri runs NVIDIA's global sales and field organisation, which sells the GPUs and systems behind the AI data-center boom. He joined NVIDIA in 2005 after 22 years at Sun Microsystems in sales, marketing and general management. His wealth comes from NVIDIA stock (about 0.02% stake), and he remains in the role as of 2026.
interesting_fact: Puri holds about 0.02% of NVIDIA, which in October 2025 became the first company ever worth $5 trillion. That was enough to make a sales executive a billionaire on Forbes' real-time list.
deep_cut_fact: Before his 22 years at Sun, Puri worked in product development at Texas Instruments and in consulting at Booz Allen. He holds electrical engineering degrees from the University of Minnesota (BS) and Caltech (MS) as well as a Harvard MBA, so he is an engineer by training, not a career salesman.
notes: Low public profile with no NVIDIA newsroom bio page, so requests are best routed through NVIDIA corporate communications. SEC filer CIK 0001347842 ('Puri Ajay K'). Forbes now marks him as 'former' on its real-time list.

name: Eddy Sugianto
current_role: President Commissioner, PT Prima Andalan Mandiri Tbk (IDX: MCOL, 'Mandiri Coal'); controlling shareholder of Mandiri Herindo Adiperkasa (Mandiri Services)
profile: Indonesian coal magnate behind the Mandiri group, whose PT Mandiri Intiperkasa mine in North Kalimantan sells coal under the 'Mandiri Coal' brand, with in-house mining contracting and barging units. He took Prima Andalan Mandiri public in 2021 and the coal-services arm in 2023; his family controls ~70% of MCOL. Brother Handy Glivirgo is president director.
interesting_fact: Detik dubbed him one of Indonesia's 'OKB' (new rich) when he debuted on Forbes' billionaire list with US$1.2B; Mandiri Coal hit record output of 9.02 million tonnes in 2022.

notes: Very low media profile; no personal accounts found. Best route is MCOL's corporate secretary. Commissioner-since-2005 detail from Detik.

name: Lee Chae-yoon
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Leeno Industrial (KOSDAQ: 058470), Busan
profile: Lee Chae-yoon (b. 1950, Namhae County) founded Leeno Industrial in 1978, nine years after finishing technical high school in Busan. Leeno makes IC test sockets and 'Leeno Pin' probes that check chips for defects, for more than 1,000 customers including Nvidia, Samsung, SK Hynix and TSMC. AI-driven demand made him a billionaire in 2024; he owns about 35% of the company.
interesting_fact: The company name combines his surname with his wife's. Leeno was the first Korean maker of semiconductor test sockets and probes, which were entirely imported until the 1980s. 'Leeno Pin' is now the industry's generic word for test probes, with about 70% global share.
deep_cut_fact: A self-made engineer who kept studying: he finished Kwangsung (Kyeongsung) Engineering High School in 1969, founded Leeno in 1978, and earned his Dong-Eui University degree only in 1991, 13 years after starting the company. He later completed a KAIST executive programme.
notes: Low media profile; rarely gives interviews. Route via Leeno's general company email or contact page in Busan. Korean-language outreach is advisable. Forbes source: https://www.forbes.com/sites/johnkang/2024/03/14/founder-of-chip-testing-firm-rides-ai-boom-to-become-south-koreas-newest-billionaire/

name: Toby Neugebauer
current_role: Co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi Inc. (FRMI); former CEO (left April 2026); co-owner of MLS club Austin FC
profile: West Texas-born energy investor (NYU BBA '93) who worked at Kidder Peabody, co-founded Windrock Energy (sold to Macquarie) and in 1998 co-founded Quantum Energy Partners, running five funds. In 2025 he co-founded Fermi America to build 'Project Matador', a multi-gigawatt private power grid and AI data-center campus near Amarillo, and took it public in Oct 2025.
interesting_fact: Fermi's Project Matador in the Texas Panhandle was pitched as one of the world's largest energy-and-data campuses, combining gas, nuclear, solar and grid power to serve hyperscale AI tenants.
deep_cut_fact: Outside energy, his philanthropy has focused on family formation in US inner cities, and abroad he has worked with orphanages in China and helped build and maintain schools in Rwanda and Zambia.
notes: Sensitive timing: he left Fermi as CEO in April 2026, was removed from the board, and has been in a public proxy fight with the company (calling for a sale/special meeting). Avoid the dispute in outreach; his PR firm Collected Strategies issues his statements. Fermi IR is not a good route for him now.

name: Fang Xiaoling
current_role: Founder, Chairman and controlling shareholder, Maxio Technology (Hangzhou) Co. (STAR Market: 688449).
profile: Fang Xiaoling (b. 1963, US citizen) holds Zhejiang University BS/MS degrees and a University of Utah EE PhD. After co-founding Taiwanese fabless firm JMicron, she founded Maxio in Hangzhou in 2014; it designs SSD/data-storage controller chips and AIoT signal-processing chips, and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in late 2024. She controls ~45% of Maxio.
interesting_fact: Surveillance giant Hikvision invested in Maxio in its third year and became its 2nd-largest shareholder (37% with a subsidiary pre-IPO); Maxio's controllers are mass-deployed at YMTC and Longsys.
deep_cut_fact: Before chips for storage, she was a principal engineer at Sonic Innovations, a Salt Lake City hearing-aid maker (then ranked world No. 7), from 1995-2001 right after her Utah PhD; she then cofounded JMicron and ran JMicron USA for 15 years.
notes: Low media profile; best route is Maxio IR (board secretary/CFO Qian Xiaofei). Data-center angle: enterprise SSD controllers.

name: Mark Armenante
current_role: Private investor; early backer and former director of Veeva Systems (2007-2015); co-founder/board member of Vlocity (acquired by Salesforce 2020) per aggregator listings
profile: A veteran of enterprise sales in pharma software, Armenante worked at Information Resources Inc. and Oracle, ran PharmaSystems, and spent over ten years as a Siebel Systems group VP. In 2007 he became one of Veeva's first outside backers and directors. He held about 13% of Veeva before its 2013 IPO, the source of his fortune.
interesting_fact: Veeva's 2013 S-1 shows he owned 14.8 million shares (13.2%) before the IPO, nearly as many as CEO Peter Gassner's 15.2 million. That made him one of the company's largest individual holders.
deep_cut_fact: Long before Veeva, he was President of PharmaSystems, Inc., a pharmaceutical sales-force management company, from 1991 to 1994. That is essentially the market Veeva later dominated. He also holds a biology degree from Case Western Reserve University.
notes: He was about 74 in 2026 (61 at the S-1 in 2013), and I found no recent public activity or confirmation that he is alive. He has no public social or website presence, and some aggregator claims (e.g., 'founder' of Veeva) are imprecise. He was a Series A investor and director rather than an operating co-founder.

name: Ray Irani
current_role: Retired; former Chairman & CEO of Occidental Petroleum (1990-2011); reported as chairman/CEO of private investment firm Ray Investment, LLC
profile: Lebanese-born chemist (b. 1935) who worked at Monsanto and was president/COO of Olin before Armand Hammer brought him to Occidental in 1983; Hammer named him heir in 1990 and he led Oxy for two decades, growing it into a major US oil producer. He stepped down as CEO in 2011 and as chairman in 2013 and has since kept a low profile.
interesting_fact: Armand Hammer, then 91, picked Irani as his successor at Occidental in February 1990; by 1988 Irani's team was already running day-to-day operations for the nonagenarian founder.
deep_cut_fact: He earned a chemistry BS from the American University of Beirut in 1953, moved to Los Angeles at 18 and had a USC physical-chemistry PhD by 1957; USC named its life sciences building Ray R. Irani Hall in 2007, and he was elected to the National Academy of Engineering in 2012 for work on particulate systems.
notes: Aged ~91; no death reported in searches as of Nov 2026 (Wikipedia lists him as living) - verify before outreach. No published personal or office contact found. Possible routes: AUB trustees emeriti page (https://www.aub.edu.lb/AboutUs/bot/emeriti/Pages/irani.aspx) or USC. Avoid executive-pay and tax-shelter controversies.

name: Cao Jianwei
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Zhejiang Jingsheng Mechanical & Electrical (SZSE: 300316); co-actual controller with founder Qiu Minxiu
profile: Cao Jianwei (曹建伟, b. 1978), an engineering PhD, has run Jingsheng since its early years (GM from 2010, chairman since 2016). Founded in 2006 by Zhejiang University professor Qiu Minxiu, it makes crystal-growth furnaces for solar and semiconductor silicon plus sapphire and SiC substrates; listed in Shenzhen in 2012.
interesting_fact: Jingsheng's founder, his co-controller Qiu Minxiu, was a Zhejiang University professor who retired at 60 to start the company and rang the bell for its ChiNext IPO at 67.
deep_cut_fact: A researcher in hydraulic transmission and electromechanical control, he has won two first-class Zhejiang Provincial Science & Technology awards, and was named one of Shaoxing's Top Ten Outstanding Young People and a recipient of the Chinese Red Cross Humanitarian Service Medal.
notes: Engineer-chairman; few English-language interviews. Data-center/AI angle via semiconductor equipment and SiC substrates (power electronics). Route via company securities office.

name: Kiki Barki
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder, PT Harum Energy Tbk (IDX: HRUM); owner of private coal miner Tanito Harum
profile: Indonesian coal pioneer Kiki Barki (Ji Qihui) founded Tanito Harum in 1988 and Harum Energy in 1995, listing Harum in 2010. His sons now run Harum, which has diversified from Kalimantan thermal coal into nickel, including a stake in ASX-listed Nickel Industries with nickel pig-iron plants in Indonesia.
interesting_fact: Then-mining minister Ginandjar Kartasasmita recalled that Barki spoke Mandarin better than Indonesian, having lived and studied in China for more than 10 years before returning to set up Tanito Harum, one of the few Indonesian-owned coal miners of the late 1980s.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Bandung in 1939 to a Hokchia (Fujian) family, he finished secondary school in Beijing and trained at a mining academy there; before coal he helped run his father's textile, hotel and banking businesses, and in 1993 his interests backed PT Vietmindo Energitama, a coal mine in northern Vietnam.
notes: Aged ~87; alive status based on Forbes' 2026 profile wording, not independently confirmed (web-search budget ran out). Very private; day-to-day leadership is with his sons at Harum. harumenergy.com is behind bot protection, so its IR/corporate secretary contact could not be extracted - check its Investor Relations page manually.

name: Sean Lie
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Technology Officer, Cerebras Systems (Nasdaq: CBRS)
profile: MIT-trained chip architect and one of Cerebras' five co-founders, who all came from SeaMicro (sold to AMD in 2012). As CTO since 2022 he leads the technology behind the Wafer-Scale Engine, a dinner-plate-sized AI chip, and Cerebras' inference cloud and data centers. Cerebras listed on Nasdaq in May 2026; his roughly 5.3M pre-IPO shares are the source of his wealth.
interesting_fact: Cerebras' May 2026 IPO raised $5.55B at $185 a share, the largest U.S. tech IPO since 2019. The stock opened at $350, valuing the wafer-scale chipmaker at about $95B.
deep_cut_fact: Before Cerebras, Lie was a microprocessor architect on AMD's advanced architecture team (2004-08). At SeaMicro he was lead hardware architect of the IO-virtualization fabric ASIC that linked hundreds of tiny CPUs in its dense servers, and after AMD bought SeaMicro he was Chief Architect for Data Center Server Solutions.
notes: Core AI/data-center guest. He often gives technical talks (e.g. at Hot Chips) on the WSE architecture. The X and LinkedIn listed are Cerebras corporate accounts, not his. Media route is pr@cerebras.ai; the general inbox is info@cerebras.ai.

name: Lee Man Chun
current_role: Chairman and founder, Lee & Man Paper Manufacturing Ltd. (HKEX: 2314)
profile: Raymond Lee Man Chun founded and chairs Lee & Man Paper, a Hong Kong-listed maker of containerboard, tissue and pulp with ~10,000 staff and mills in mainland China and Vietnam. A UBC engineering graduate, he is a CPPCC National Committee member, holds the Silver Bauhinia Star and is an INED of Beijing Enterprises Water.
interesting_fact: He was named a Hong Kong Young Industrialist (2002) and one of Hong Kong's Ten Outstanding Young Persons (2003), and is an honorary citizen of both Dongguan and Changshu, where Lee & Man runs major mills.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training: he holds a B.A.Sc. (applied science) from the University of British Columbia, which also awarded him an honorary Doctor of Laws in 2014. He chairs the Bai Ren (百仁) Foundation and joined City University of Hong Kong's Council in 2015.
notes: The SEC insider link in the input (TSMC SVP) is almost certainly a name-collision with a different person - ignore it. Company switchboard 852-2319-9889 (Lee & Man Commercial Centre, North Point). Company website was down/unreachable during research; no published press email found. Web search budget ran out while researching this person; bio from 10jqka HK executive profiles.

June 1963) is the founder and president of China Gas Holdings, one of China's largest cross-regional city-gas distributors, piping natural gas to households and industry in hundreds of Chinese cities and expanding into LPG, integrated energy and renewables. name: Zhang Qin
current_role: Executive Director, Vice Chairman, Deputy General Manager and Board Secretary, SG Micro Corp (300661.SZ / 03661.HK)
profile: Zhang Qin co-founded SG Micro (圣邦微电子), a Beijing analog-chip designer started in January 2007 with chairman Zhang Shilong. It is China's No. 1 domestic analog IC company by revenue and No. 8 globally. Listed in Shenzhen (2017) and Hong Kong (2026), it is part-owned by her: she holds about 8% and belongs to the controlling group.
interesting_fact: SG Micro makes the signal-chain and power-management chips (amplifiers, converters, drivers) that sit in nearly every electronic system. 2025 revenue was about RMB 4.0bn, and Q1 2026 net profit roughly doubled year on year.
deep_cut_fact: She trained as an engineer: in July 1993 she earned an engineering bachelor's from the Beijing Institute of Light Industry (now Beijing Technology and Business University). She has been on SG Micro's board since its first month in January 2007 and has also been board secretary since 2012.
notes: As board secretary she oversees SG Micro's investor relations, so the IR email effectively reaches her office. Low personal media profile. Chairman/CEO Zhang Shilong is the public face of the company.

name: Lu Xinchun
current_role: Chief Scientist, Hwatsing Technology (华海清科, SSE STAR: 688120); Chief Researcher, Dept. of Mechanical Engineering, Tsinghua University
profile: Tsinghua tribologist (b. 1966, Yantai) whose team began chemical-mechanical polishing (CMP) research in 2000 and spun it out in 2013 as Hwatsing, now China's No.1 domestic CMP and wafer-thinning equipment maker, listed on the STAR Market in 2022. He was chairman until 2025 and remains chief scientist guiding R&D.
interesting_fact: His team launched China's first 12-inch CMP tool with domestic IP and an integrated grinding-polishing thinning tool, key equipment for chipmaking and advanced packaging; he won a 2025 Ho Leung Ho Lee Science and Technology Innovation Prize.
deep_cut_fact: An academic first: he earned his bachelor's and master's at Jilin University of Technology (1988, 1991), a PhD at the CAS Institute of Metal Research (1994), and did his postdoc at Tsinghua's State Key Laboratory of Tribology, the field of nano-scale friction behind CMP.
notes: Academic-founder; stepped down as Hwatsing chairman in 2025 (Wang Tongqing is now chairman & GM) but remains chief scientist (https://www.cls.cn/detail/2273649). Routes: Hwatsing board office (secretary Chen Zhenyin) or Tsinghua Mechanical Engineering dept. Likely Chinese-language outreach needed.

name: Le Weiping
current_role: Chairman, General Manager and controlling shareholder, Shenzhen CSL Vacuum Technology (Hengyunchang, STAR Market: 688785).
profile: Le Weiping (b. 1973) spent ~11 years at US plasma-power maker Advanced Energy in Shenzhen and Shanghai before founding CSL Vacuum (Hengyunchang) to localise plasma RF power systems for chip equipment. Its main customer is Piotech; the company listed on Shanghai's STAR Market on 28 Jan 2026. He controls ~73% of voting rights (wealth shared with Cao Li per Hurun).
interesting_fact: He quit a well-paid multinational job in 2013, when China's chip-equipment sector was nascent, and started CSL with five employees in an office under 100 square metres in Shenzhen's Bao'an district.
deep_cut_fact: His first job was as a technician/engineer at the telecom-equipment factory of the Taoyuan County Post & Telecom Bureau in Hunan; he joined Advanced Energy Shenzhen in 2003 as a test technician and rose to product-applications engineer and senior sales manager in Shanghai.
notes: Recent IPO (Jan 2026); low personal media profile. Board secretary Zhuang Lihua handles IR. Relationship to co-listed Cao Li not confirmed.

name: Cao Li
current_role: Major shareholder (back-office management), Shenzhen CSL Vacuum Science & Technology (恒运昌, STAR 688785)
profile: Co-owner, with chairman Le Weiping, of Shenzhen CSL Vacuum Science & Technology, which makes plasma RF power supplies and related core components for semiconductor process equipment. The company listed on Shanghai's STAR Market on 28 Jan 2026, which put the couple on the 2026 Hurun China list. Per IPO disclosures she handles back-office management rather than operations.
interesting_fact: CSL was started in Shenzhen's Bao'an district with just five staff after Le Weiping spent 11 years at US plasma-power firm Advanced Energy; it now aims to be a platform supplier of plasma-process core components for China's chip-tool makers.

name: Green Chang-Lin
current_role: Chairman, MPI Corporation (旺矽科技, TWSE: 6223), Hsinchu, Taiwan
profile: Ko Chang-lin (葛長林; listed by Hurun as 'Green Chang-Lin') started out in semiconductor equipment distribution and built MPI Corporation, now described as the world's fourth-largest probe-card maker. AI-chip testing demand has pushed MPI to record results, sold-out capacity and ~6-month lead times.
interesting_fact: With AI-chip test demand outstripping capacity, MPI in 2026 began asking customers to pay before taking delivery, which he called a first for the probe-card industry.
deep_cut_fact: He also chairs Gordon Biersch Taiwan (吉比鮮釀). He won the brewpub franchise after a meeting in the US was postponed and he spent the evening tasting 10+ experimental beers with the brewer until midnight; the first Taipei outlet opened in 2008. He says it made him no money but 10+ years of happiness.
notes: Listed with country China (Hurun) but he is Taiwan-based. Strong AI/data-center supply chain angle (probe cards for AI ASIC/GPU testing). Mandarin-language media interviews are common; route via MPI IR.

name: Jones Chen
current_role: Chairman, Genius Electronic Optical Co. (GSEO, TWSE: 3406), Taichung, Taiwan
profile: Chen Tien-ching (陳天慶, 'Jones Chen') leads Genius Electronic Optical, a Taiwanese maker of precision plastic lenses for smartphone cameras (a major Apple supplier), founded 1990 and listed 2005. Under him GSEO is expanding into smart-glasses optics, humanoid-robot lenses and data-center optical interconnects / co-packaged optics.
interesting_fact: In Oct 2026 3M agreed to take a ~4.7% stake in GSEO via private placement and partner on 3M's Expanded Beam Optical (EBO) connectors for hyperscale AI data centers; GSEO plans staged mass production of co-packaged-optics parts in 2027-2028.
deep_cut_fact: In the mid-2000s he was GSEO's general manager under his elder brother Chen Tien-shu (then chairman); the two brothers quietly went to Xiamen to invest in and build the factories that became the company's main production base.
notes: Taiwanese (Hurun lists him under China). Speaks at GSEO earnings calls; little personal press. Strong data-center angle via CPO/optical interconnect pivot. IR contact is a named IR officer published on the company IR page. Deep-cut source (Global Views 2006) could not be fetched directly; verify before use.

name: Wu Zuyu
current_role: Founder and chairman, Xiamen Hithium Energy Storage Technology (海辰储能)
profile: Wu Zuyu (吴祖钰), born in the mid-1980s, holds an applied-chemistry BSc from Shandong Normal University and a chemical-engineering MSc from Fuzhou University. He was an engineer at CATL before founding Hithium in Xiamen on 27 Dec 2019. Within about six years Hithium became one of the world's top three makers of stationary storage batteries, passing 100 GWh of shipments, and it is pursuing a Hong Kong IPO.
interesting_fact: Hithium went from founding to roughly third in global energy-storage cell shipments in about five years. Hurun valued it at RMB 25bn in 2024, and it now sells 5 MWh containers and 8-hour long-duration storage systems in the US, Australia and Japan.
deep_cut_fact: As a CATL engineer he was first-named inventor on a run of energy-storage patents covering current collectors, electrode sheets and cells. One count puts it at 67 such patents between 2012 and 2018.
notes: Very low public profile; Hithium's prospectus is the main source on him. The press email comes from an older Hithium newsroom release and may be outdated. Avoid the topic of CATL in outreach: there are ongoing non-compete and unfair-competition disputes, which also delayed the HK IPO. The 67-patent count is from 36kr (https://www.36kr.com/p/2541517764011779).

name: Wei Jisheng
current_role: Chairman, Longkou Shengtong Group; major shareholder (27.7%) and long-time director of Senton Energy / Shengtong Energy (SZSE: 001331)
profile: Wei Jisheng (b. 1963) built a trucking business in Longkou, Shandong into Senton (Shengtong) Energy, an LNG trading and tank-truck logistics firm ranked 5th in China for both LNG trading and LNG transport in 2025, listed in Shenzhen. In 2026 his family sold control (~45% incl. tender offer) to Qiteng Robotics; he still held 27.73% at mid-2026.
interesting_fact: Senton Energy trucks LNG from CNOOC/Sinopec/PetroChina coastal terminals and inland liquefaction plants to customers nationwide; its LNG sales revenue grew 18.6% to about RMB 5.47bn in H1 2026 (per its filings), and control passed in June 2026 to a robotics company.
deep_cut_fact: He started work in December 1978, aged 15, as a staff member of the Huang County Transport Company's Longkou motor team, rising to team leader and then manager of Longkou No.3 Motor Transport Co. before founding Shengtong Transport in 1994.
notes: Low public profile; no interviews found. Since June 2026 the controlling shareholder is Qiteng Robotics (actual controller Zhu Dong); board was re-elected early in 2026, so check whether Wei remains a director. Route via company board office mailbox.

name: Jacob DeWitte
current_role: Co-Founder and CEO, Oklo Inc. (NYSE: OKLO)
profile: Nuclear engineer (Univ. of Florida BS 2008; MIT SM/PhD) who worked at Sandia, Urenco USA, the Naval Nuclear Laboratory and GE (core design lead on the PRISM sodium fast reactor) before co-founding Oklo in 2013 with Caroline Cochran (COO). Oklo, developing small advanced fission 'powerhouses' aimed partly at data centers, listed in 2024 via a Sam Altman-backed SPAC.
interesting_fact: Oklo is named after the uranium deposits at Oklo, Gabon, where natural self-sustaining fission reactions occurred about two billion years ago; DeWitte also raised the first modern institutional VC-led financing of a fission company.
deep_cut_fact: Growing up in Albuquerque, he spent weekends with his dad getting donuts and visiting the National Nuclear Science Museum; his favourite exhibit was a simulated fuel pellet the size of a pencil eraser holding the energy of a ton of coal. He later talked his family into detouring to Arizona's nuclear plant on a Grand Canyon trip.
notes: Highly relevant (nuclear for data centers). Frequent conference speaker (CERAWeek etc.) and congressional witness; 2014 Forbes 30 Under 30 (Energy). Oklo's site lists investors@oklo.com as its single media/investor contact; company X is @oklo. UF 2021 Distinguished Early Career Alumni Award: https://mse.ufl.edu/jacob-dewitte-2021-distinguished-early-career-alumni-award/

profile: Liu Manshi (刘满世) and family control Manshi Group, a private thermal-coal producer in Jungar Banner, Ordos, Inner Mongolia, which says it runs 8 large modern mines producing 25M+ tonnes of low-ash, low-sulphur steam coal a year plus a 1,000-truck logistics and sales network. notes: Low-profile engineer-founder; route via IR (board secretary Yang Biao). Chinese-language outreach advisable. Relevant angle: Chinese power-management chips for servers/HPC.

name: Gao Jiyang
current_role: Founder & CEO, Galaxea AI (星海图, GALAXEA (Beijing) Artificial Intelligence Technology Co.)
profile: Gao Jiyang (高继扬) studied microelectronics at Tsinghua (2015) and earned a USC PhD in computer vision (2018), then was a tech lead at Waymo and an executive director at Momenta. He founded embodied-AI/robotics company Galaxea AI with Tsinghua's Hang Zhao; it builds general-purpose humanoid and wheeled-arm robots plus its own G0 foundation models, and became a unicorn.

deep_cut_fact: At Waymo he was co-first author of VectorNet (CVPR 2020), an influential method for encoding HD maps and agent motion for trajectory prediction, and of TNT (CoRL 2020) with his future Galaxea cofounder Hang Zhao.
notes: Personal email is self-published (written 'jiyanggao1203 at gmail dot com') on his academic homepage, which dates from his Momenta days, so may be less monitored. Robotics rather than data centers, but strong AI-infrastructure/foundation-model angle.

name: Che Chengju
current_role: Second-largest shareholder (~4.3%) of Zibo Qixiang Tengda Chemical (002408.SZ); former chairman and later director/GM, no longer listed among current management
profile: Che Chengju (车成聚, b. 1950), a Qilu Petrochemical veteran, from 1998 built Qixiang into a Zibo C4-chemicals producer, listed in Shenzhen in 2010. After the parent group's restructuring, state-owned Shandong Energy took control (2022); he stepped down as chairman in 2023 and remains a major individual shareholder.
